1.191.m: Homage to holy Gaṇeśa.
Now begins the table of contents of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara Mahāpurāṇa.
First book 1.
1. Introduction to the narrative.
2. Production of Hiraṇyagarbha by Nārāyaṇa, though bodiless, out of a desire to create the worlds.
3. The uplifting of the earth by the blessed Viṣṇu in the form of a boar.
4. Declaration of the subterranean realms—Kālāgnirudra, Pātāla, Sutala, Ābhāsatala, and others—and of their inhabitants.
5. Description of the seven worlds beginning with Bhūḥ, of the seven atmospheric wind-regions and the like therein, and of their inhabitants.
6. Declaration of the greatness of Śvetadvīpa in the midst of the Ocean of Milk on the occasion of describing the earth-disc with its shape and dimensions.

1.191.s: 7 jambūdvīpe himavadādikulaparvatavarṇanaprasaṅge sumerorvistṛtavarṇanam, hemakūṭottarato harivarṣādyabhidhānānantaraṃ kulaparvateṣu krameṇa yakṣadaityagandharvādīnāṃ vihārabhūmitvābhidhānam ...
1.191.d: 7 जम्बूद्वीपे हिमवदादिकुलपर्वतवर्णनप्रसङ्गे सुमेरोर्विस्तृतवर्णनम्, हेमकूटोत्तरतो हरिवर्षाद्यभिधानानन्तरं कुलपर्वतेषु क्रमेण यक्षदैत्यगन्धर्वादीनां विहारभूमित्वाभिधानम् ॥।
1.191.m: 7. Detailed description of Sumeru on the occasion of describing the principal mountain ranges beginning with the Himavat in Jambūdvīpa; declaration of Harivarṣa and others to the north of Hemakūṭa, followed by the declaration that the principal mountain ranges are successive pleasure grounds of the Yakṣas, Daityas, Gandharvas, and others.

1.191.s: 8 navavidhabhāratavarṣasyāṣṭamahāgiricchannatvābhidhānapurassaraṃ bhārate kṛtasu- kṛtasyaivetareṣu ramyavasatiṣu kimpuruṣādivarṣeṣu nivāsakathanam
1.191.d: 8 नवविधभारतवर्षस्याष्टमहागिरिच्छन्नत्वाभिधानपुरस्सरं भारते कृतसु- कृतस्यैवेतरेषु रम्यवसतिषु किम्पुरुषादिवर्षेषु निवासकथनम्
1.191.m: 8. Account preceded by the declaration that the ninefold Bhāratavarṣa is encompassed by eight great mountains, of the dwelling of only one who has performed good deeds in Bhārata within the other pleasant habitations, the realms beginning with Kimpuruṣa.
9. Description of the realms beginning with Pāñcāla.
10. Description of the rivers issuing from the seven principal mountain ranges beginning with Mahendra and Malaya.
11. Description of the rivers originating from the snowy mountain.
12. Narrative in praise of Kosala.
13. Description of Ayodhyā.
14. Praise of Ikṣvāku, son of Manu.
15. Narrative of the slaying of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, and the name Medinī given to the earth because of its origin from their fat.

1.191.s: 16 bhārgavottaṃkamunitapaḥprasannena viṣṇunā tasmā icchājalotpādanaśaktipradānantadanumatena bṛhadaśvena rājñā kuvalāśvaśarīrāntaḥpraviṣṭabhagavatsāhyenodakarākṣasasya dhundhorhananaṃ svasya dhundhumārāhvaprasiddhilābhaśca ...
1.191.d: 16 भार्गवोत्तंकमुनितपःप्रसन्नेन विष्णुना तस्मा इच्छाजलोत्पादनशक्तिप्रदानन्तदनुमतेन बृहदश्वेन राज्ञा कुवलाश्वशरीरान्तःप्रविष्टभगवत्साह्येनोदकराक्षसस्य धुन्धोर्हननं स्वस्य धुन्धुमाराह्वप्रसिद्धिलाभश्च ॥।
1.191.m: 16. Viṣṇu, pleased by the austerities of the Bhārgava sage Uttaṅka, granting him the power to produce water at will; by his permission, King Bṛhadaśva, through the help of the Blessed One who entered the body of Kuvalāśva, slaying the water-demon Dhundhu and attaining his own fame under the name Dhundhumāra.

1.191.s: 17 dhundhumāravaṃśīyanṛpativarṇanaprasaṅge strīmṛgayādivyasanalampaṭabāhurājasya haihayatālajaṅghādinṛpaiḥparājayādaraṇye sagarotpattyavasāne pañcatvaprāpte- ścyavanena sagarasya dhanurādividyāpāragāmitvādiyogyatāpādanānantaraṃ dāragrahādyāpādanam –
1.191.d: 17 धुन्धुमारवंशीयनृपतिवर्णनप्रसङ्गे स्त्रीमृगयादिव्यसनलम्पटबाहुराजस्य हैहयतालजङ्घादिनृपैःपराजयादरण्ये सगरोत्पत्त्यवसाने पञ्चत्वप्राप्ते- श्च्यवनेन सगरस्य धनुरादिविद्यापारगामित्वादियोग्यतापादनानन्तरं दारग्रहाद्यापादनम् –
1.191.m: 17. On the occasion of describing the kings of Dhundhumāra's lineage, King Bāhu, addicted to vices such as women and hunting, is defeated by kings such as the Haihayas and Tālajaṅghas, and attains death in the wilderness upon the birth of Sagara; whereupon Cyavana imparts to Sagara eligibility through complete mastery in archery and the other sciences, followed by his marriage and other accomplishments.

1.191.s: 18 sagaranṛpavisṛṣṭāśvamedhīyaturagamapahṛtya kapilena svāśrame pātāle tanni rodhaḥ; tadanveṣaṇavyāpṛtaṣaṣṭisahasrasagarasutānāṃ svanikhātasāgaramārgeṇa pātālagamanaṃ kapilaśāpena bhasmībhavanañca, tadanveṣaṇapravṛttāṃśumatā santoṣitakapilatastvatpautro bhagīrathastaduddhārārthaṃ svargaṅgāmāneṣyatīti varaprāptiḥ ...
1.191.d: 18 सगरनृपविसृष्टाश्वमेधीयतुरगमपहृत्य कपिलेन स्वाश्रमे पाताले तन्नि रोधः; तदन्वेषणव्यापृतषष्टिसहस्रसगरसुतानां स्वनिखातसागरमार्गेण पातालगमनं कपिलशापेन भस्मीभवनञ्च, तदन्वेषणप्रवृत्तांशुमता सन्तोषितकपिलतस्त्वत्पौत्रो भगीरथस्तदुद्धारार्थं स्वर्गङ्गामानेष्यतीति वरप्राप्तिः ॥।
1.191.m: 18. Kapilá steals the sacrificial horse released for the horse-sacrifice by King Sagara and detains it at his hermitage in Pātāla; the sixty thousand sons of Sagara, engaged in searching for it, go to Pātāla along the path of the ocean dug by themselves and are reduced to ashes by Kapila's curse; Aṃśumat, setting out in search of them, propitiates Kapila and obtains the boon that his grandson Bhagīratha will bring the celestial Gaṅgā to deliver them.

1.191.s: 19 pitryuddhārakāmabhagīrathasya sahasravarṣatapohaṣṭagaṅgādeśānusāraṃ viyatastanni- pātavegasahanakṣamaśaṅkarārādhanānte tatkaparde gaṅgānipātaḥ, aho prakhara- vegāyā mama sahanaṃ kathaṃ maheśvaraḥ soḍhetyavaliptāyāstasyā hareṇa sajaṭājūṭe tirodhānam, tadanu ciratapaḥkliṣṭabhagīrathānukampayā tasyāstyāgaḥ prācyādiṣu saptadhā tadgatiśca ...
1.191.d: 19 पित्र्युद्धारकामभगीरथस्य सहस्रवर्षतपोहष्टगङ्गादेशानुसारं वियतस्तन्नि- पातवेगसहनक्षमशङ्कराराधनान्ते तत्कपर्दे गङ्गानिपातः, अहो प्रखर- वेगाया मम सहनं कथं महेश्वरः सोढेत्यवलिप्तायास्तस्या हरेण सजटाजूटे तिरोधानम्, तदनु चिरतपःक्लिष्टभगीरथानुकम्पया तस्यास्त्यागः प्राच्यादिषु सप्तधा तद्गतिश्च ॥।
1.191.m: 19. Bhagīratha, desiring the deliverance of his ancestors, according to the instruction of Gaṅgā who was delighted by a thousand years of austerity, propitiates Śaṅkara who is able to bear the momentum of her fall from the sky; the Gaṅgā falls into his matted locks; filled with conceit—'Ah, how can Maheśvara endure me who have such a fierce torrent?'—she is hidden away by Hara in his mass of matted locks; thereafter, out of compassion for Bhagīratha who had suffered long austerities, he releases her, and she courses in seven streams toward the east and other quarters.

1.191.s: 20 kānyakubje yajñadīkṣitasya jahnorāśramaplāvanāttena yogabalena gaṅgāyāḥ pānaṃ munyanunayena karṇatastyāgo duhitṛtve kalpanañca ( ata eva jāhnavītvam) ...
1.191.d: 20 कान्यकुब्जे यज्ञदीक्षितस्य जह्नोराश्रमप्लावनात्तेन योगबलेन गङ्गायाः पानं मुन्यनुनयेन कर्णतस्त्यागो दुहितृत्वे कल्पनञ्च ( अत एव जाह्नवीत्वम्) ॥।
1.191.m: 20. Jahnu, consecrated for a sacrifice in Kānyakubja, has his hermitage flooded, and drinks up the Gaṅgā by the power of yoga; upon the sage being placated, she is released through his ear and is reckoned as his daughter (hence her status as Jāhnavī).

1.191.s: 21 svāyambhuve'ntare bāṣkali (bali) rājena viśvabhugindrapadamapahṛtam, punarindrasya svārājyalabdhaye'dbhutavāmanarūpamugdhabāṣkalinendraprārthanayā vāmanāya tripadabhūmidānapratijñāne taddakṣiṇacaraṇākramaṇena śakrasya svarājyalābho viṣṇupadāgrakṣatāṇḍapraviṣṭapavitrajalasya viṣṇupadītvam
1.191.d: 21 स्वायम्भुवेऽन्तरे बाष्कलि (बलि) राजेन विश्वभुगिन्द्रपदमपहृतम्, पुनरिन्द्रस्य स्वाराज्यलब्धयेऽद्भुतवामनरूपमुग्धबाष्कलिनेन्द्रप्रार्थनया वामनाय त्रिपदभूमिदानप्रतिज्ञाने तद्दक्षिणचरणाक्रमणेन शक्रस्य स्वराज्यलाभो विष्णुपदाग्रक्षताण्डप्रविष्टपवित्रजलस्य विष्णुपदीत्वम्
1.191.m: 21. In the Svāyambhuva manvantara, King Bāṣkali (Bali) usurped the status of Indra Viśvabhuk; then, so that Indra might regain his sovereignty, Bāṣkali, enchanted by the wondrous Vāmana form, upon Indra's request pledged to give three paces of land to Vāmana; through the stride of his right foot Śakra regained his sovereignty, and the holy water that entered the cosmic egg pierced by the tip of Viṣṇu's foot became the Viṣṇupadī.

22. The Gaṅgā issuing forth from the cosmic egg, pervading the world of Viṣṇu, Tapas, Mahas, the lunar sphere, all the realms, the continents, and the seven subterranean regions, and re-entering the cosmic egg.
23. Description of the lineage of the royal sage Bhagīratha, followed by a particular description of the prowess of Kārttavīrya.

1.191.s: 24 vṛttrāsuraviśvarūpa ( brahma )hatyābhītavāsavasya mānase sarasi bisatantau līnatvānnahuṣasyendratā, śacīkāmukamunivāhyāśibikārūḍhasya tasyā- gastyaśāpātsarpatā, bhāviyudhiṣṭhirasākṣātkāre śāpavimokṣaḥ, devarājā- bhāve dharmaviplavānmarakādyupadravācca pralīnasvāhāsvadhāvaṣaṭakāre trida- śaprārthitaharyanugrahādindrasya punaḥ svārājyalābhe sarvalokaśāntiḥ
1.191.d: 24 वृत्त्रासुरविश्वरूप ( ब्रह्म )हत्याभीतवासवस्य मानसे सरसि बिसतन्तौ लीनत्वान्नहुषस्येन्द्रता, शचीकामुकमुनिवाह्याशिबिकारूढस्य तस्या- गस्त्यशापात्सर्पता, भावियुधिष्ठिरसाक्षात्कारे शापविमोक्षः, देवराजा- भावे धर्मविप्लवान्मरकाद्युपद्रवाच्च प्रलीनस्वाहास्वधावषटकारे त्रिद- शप्रार्थितहर्यनुग्रहादिन्द्रस्य पुनः स्वाराज्यलाभे सर्वलोकशान्तिः
1.191.m: 24. Vāsava, terrified of the murder of a brahmin in the slaying of the demon Vṛtra and Viśvarūpa, conceals himself in a lotus fiber in the Mānasa lake, whereupon Nahuṣa obtains the status of Indra; lusting after Śacī and mounted on a palanquin borne by sages, he becomes a serpent by the curse of Agastya, his liberation from the curse to occur upon meeting Yudhiṣṭhira in the future; in the absence of the king of gods, because of the subversion of dharma and plagues of pestilence and the like, the utterances of svāhā, svadhā, and vaṣaṭ vanish; upon Indra regaining his sovereignty through the grace of Hari requested by the thirty gods, peace is restored to all the worlds.

1.191.s: 25 hariharāvatreḥ putrībhūya dattātreyadurvāsorūpeṇāvatīrṇau, tatra dattātreyeṇa vedādhyayanayajñādivinaṣṭadharmyakriyāṇāmuddharaṇaṃ kārtavīryasya daśasahasra- varṣaparyyantaṃ tapaścaraṇācchiṣyīkaraṇaṃ pracchannadaityatadāśritanṛpapīḍita- dharāyāḥ śakrasamīpagamanañca
1.191.d: 25 हरिहरावत्रेः पुत्रीभूय दत्तात्रेयदुर्वासोरूपेणावतीर्णौ, तत्र दत्तात्रेयेण वेदाध्ययनयज्ञादिविनष्टधर्म्यक्रियाणामुद्धरणं कार्तवीर्यस्य दशसहस्र- वर्षपर्य्यन्तं तपश्चरणाच्छिष्यीकरणं प्रच्छन्नदैत्यतदाश्रितनृपपीडित- धरायाः शक्रसमीपगमनञ्च
1.191.m: 25. Hari and Hara, becoming sons of Atri, descend in the forms of Dattātreya and Durvāsas; therein Dattātreya restores the destroyed righteous rites such as Vedic recitation and sacrifice; he accepts Kārtavīrya as a disciple following his practice of austerity for ten thousand years; and the earth, oppressed by disguised Daityas and the kings dependent upon them, approaches Śakra.

1.191.s: 26 nāke bhūmyā viṣṇudarśanaṃ śakraṃ prati svaduḥkhanivedanaṃ, śakreṇa tatkaṣṭa- nivāraṇārthaṃ brahmasadogamanam ...
1.191.d: 26 नाके भूम्या विष्णुदर्शनं शक्रं प्रति स्वदुःखनिवेदनं, शक्रेण तत्कष्ट- निवारणार्थं ब्रह्मसदोगमनम् ॥।
1.191.m: 26. The vision of Viṣṇu in heaven by the earth; her report of her suffering to Śakra; and Śakra's journey to the assembly of Brahmā to remove that distress.

1.191.s: 27 duṣṭakṣatriyapīḍitabhūbhāraharaṇārthaṃ bṛhaspatisahitaśakreṇa pitāmahastavanaṃ śaṃkaro vo duḥkhaṃ nivārayiṣyati tatsamīpe gacchateti tasyottaram
1.191.d: 27 दुष्टक्षत्रियपीडितभूभारहरणार्थं बृहस्पतिसहितशक्रेण पितामहस्तवनं शंकरो वो दुःखं निवारयिष्यति तत्समीपे गच्छतेति तस्योत्तरम्
1.191.m: 27. Praise of the Grandfather by Śakra accompanied by Bṛhaspati to remove the burden of the earth oppressed by wicked kṣatriyas; his reply: 'Śaṅkara will remove your suffering; go to him.'
28. The vision of Śaṃkara and the hymn of praise to him.
29. The hymn of praise to the moon uttered by Śaṃkara, the dimensions of the lunar disc, and the like.
30. The vision of the sun, the measurement of his disc, and praise of him, followed by the sun's promise to Rudra to destroy the disguised asuras, kṣatriyas, and others who followed Kārtavīrya.

1.191.s: 31 dvijaveśadhārisūryasya bhojanārthaṃ kārtikeyasakāśagamane tadanumatena sthāvarībhūtāsurāṇāṃ raviraśmiprajvalaccharaiḥ sarvadrumadāhe vaśiṣṭhāśramasyāpi dāhādbrāhmaṇo'valiptasyate (paraśurāmaḥ) bāhūṃśchetsyatīti śāpaḥ
1.191.d: 31 द्विजवेशधारिसूर्यस्य भोजनार्थं कार्तिकेयसकाशगमने तदनुमतेन स्थावरीभूतासुराणां रविरश्मिप्रज्वलच्छरैः सर्वद्रुमदाहे वशिष्ठाश्रमस्यापि दाहाद्ब्राह्मणोऽवलिप्तस्यते (परशुरामः) बाहूंश्छेत्स्यतीति शापः
1.191.m: 31. The sun in the guise of a twice-born goes to Kārtikeya to receive food; with his consent, as the asuras turned into trees are burnt along with all other trees by the flaming arrows of the sun's rays, the hermitage of Vasiṣṭha is also burnt, whereupon the curse is uttered: 'A brahmin (Paraśurāma) will cut off your arms, you arrogant one!'
32. The origin of Jamadagni, the submarine fire, and others in the lineage of Bhṛgu.

1.191.s: 33 svaparicaryāhṛṣṭapatyṛcīkalabdhavarayā satyavatyā svamātre balavattare svasyai ca brahmavarcasvidharmajñe putre vṛte svamātṛprārthanayā tayā caruviparyāsakaraṇādgarbhayorviruddhadharmatā
1.191.d: 33 स्वपरिचर्याहृष्टपत्यृचीकलब्धवरया सत्यवत्या स्वमात्रे बलवत्तरे स्वस्यै च ब्रह्मवर्चस्विधर्मज्ञे पुत्रे वृते स्वमातृप्रार्थनया तया चरुविपर्यासकरणाद्गर्भयोर्विरुद्धधर्मता
1.191.m: 33. Satyavatī, having obtained a boon from her husband Ṛcīka who was pleased by her devotion, chooses for her mother a son possessed of great strength and for herself a son endowed with brahma-splendour and knowledge of dharma; at her mother's request she exchanges the sacrificial messes, resulting in the contrary natures of the two embryos.
34. The future status of Viśvāmitra as a brahmin through the grace of the sage Cyavana.

1.191.s: 35. satyavatī jamadagnivātsyādiśataputrān, gādherbhāryā ca viśvāmitramasūta. madhyandine bane śarakrīḍāsaktajamadagniṃ patiṃ reṇukā bāṇānayanādinā paryacarat, sūryakarasantaptāṃ cirāgatāṃ tāmavalokya jamadagnau śaraiḥ sūryaṃ hantumudyukte vipramūrtidharo ravistatputratāṃ svīkṛtyacchatropānadbhayāntāmanujagrāha. sā ca sūryāṃśaputrotpatyanantaraṃ rāmaputramajījanat
1.191.d: 35. सत्यवती जमदग्निवात्स्यादिशतपुत्रान्, गाधेर्भार्या च विश्वामित्रमसूत। मध्यन्दिने बने शरक्रीडासक्तजमदग्निं पतिं रेणुका बाणानयनादिना पर्यचरत्, सूर्यकरसन्तप्तां चिरागतां तामवलोक्य जमदग्नौ शरैः सूर्यं हन्तुमुद्युक्ते विप्रमूर्तिधरो रविस्तत्पुत्रतां स्वीकृत्यच्छत्रोपानद्भयान्तामनुजग्राह। सा च सूर्यांशपुत्रोत्पत्यनन्तरं रामपुत्रमजीजनत्
1.191.m: 35. Satyavatī gave birth to a hundred sons, including Jamadagni and Vātsya, and the wife of Gādhi gave birth to Viśvāmitra. At midday, as her husband Jamadagni was engaged in archery practice in the forest, Reṇukā served him by fetching arrows and doing other tasks. Seeing her arrive late, scorched by the sun's rays, when Jamadagni prepared to slay the sun with his arrows, the Sun, assuming the form of a brahmin, accepted becoming his son and bestowed his grace upon her, who was relieved of fear, by means of an umbrella and shoes. And she, after the birth of the son who was a portion of the Sun, gave birth to the son Rāma.

1.191.s: 36 vanavihārāgatacitrāṃgarājamicchantīṃ svamātaraṃ pitrājñayā paraśurāmo'vadhīt svājñāpālanatuṣṭajamadagnistasmā icchāmaraṇavaraṃ dāśarāthirāmasākṣātkārāvadhi śastradhāritvañca vitīrya tadanurodhena tanmātaraṃ bhrātṝṃścojjīvayāmāsa, rāmaśca pitṛnideśācchaṃkaramārādhya tadanujñayā devapīḍakasaiṃhikeyānhantumiyeṣa
1.191.d: 36 वनविहारागतचित्रांगराजमिच्छन्तीं स्वमातरं पित्राज्ञया परशुरामोऽवधीत् स्वाज्ञापालनतुष्टजमदग्निस्तस्मा इच्छामरणवरं दाशराथिरामसाक्षात्कारावधि शस्त्रधारित्वञ्च वितीर्य तदनुरोधेन तन्मातरं भ्रातॄंश्चोज्जीवयामास, रामश्च पितृनिदेशाच्छंकरमाराध्य तदनुज्ञया देवपीडकसैंहिकेयान्हन्तुमियेष
1.191.m: 36. At his father's command, Paraśurāma slew his own mother, who had desired King Citrāṅga as he came strolling in the forest. Jamadagni, pleased by his obedience to his command, granted him the boon of dying when he wished, and of bearing arms until he saw Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, face to face; and at his entreaty he brought his mother and brothers back to life. Then Rāma, worshipping Śaṃkara at his father's instruction, desired by his permission to slay the Saiṃhikeyas, the tormentors of the gods.
37. Description of various portents in the abode of the Saiṃhikeyas...

1.191.s: 38 utpātakāraṇajijñāsayā pṛṣṭaśukreṇa saiṃhikekāya paraśurāmarūpiviṣṇunā naratiryagdevādiyonāvavatīrya surapatapakṣapātinā sadā daityavināśinā yuddhaṃ vihāya pātāle gantavyamiti hita upadiṣṭe saiṃhikeyena yuddhanirdhāraṇam
1.191.d: 38 उत्पातकारणजिज्ञासया पृष्टशुक्रेण सैंहिकेकाय परशुरामरूपिविष्णुना नरतिर्यग्देवादियोनाववतीर्य सुरपतपक्षपातिना सदा दैत्यविनाशिना युद्धं विहाय पाताले गन्तव्यमिति हित उपदिष्टे सैंहिकेयेन युद्धनिर्धारणम्
1.191.m: 38. When questioned by the Saiṃhikeya out of a desire to know the cause of the portents, Śukra gave beneficial counsel: 'Viṣṇu, who has assumed the form of Paraśurāma, takes descent in the wombs of men, animals, gods, and other beings, always sides with the lord of the gods, and ever destroys the Daityas; you must abandon the fight and go to the nether world.' Thereupon, the Saiṃhikeya resolved upon war.

1.191.s: 39 śukranayasamarthakaduḥsvapnasūcitadānavānvayātyayāśaṃki gaviṣṭhamatamanādṛtya viṣṇuhastena maraṇaṃ śreya iti saiṃhikeyena niścitam
1.191.d: 39 शुक्रनयसमर्थकदुःस्वप्नसूचितदानवान्वयात्ययाशंकि गविष्ठमतमनादृत्य विष्णुहस्तेन मरणं श्रेय इति सैंहिकेयेन निश्चितम्
1.191.m: 39. Disregarding the opinion of Gaviṣṭha, who feared the destruction of the lineage of the Dānavas indicated by bad dreams that supported Śukra's policy, the Saiṃhikeya decided that death at the hand of Viṣṇu was preferable.
40. When Rāhu counselled that there should be an end to enmity with Viṣṇu, there is the description of the churning of the ocean of milk and the emergence of gems such as Lakṣmī.

1.191.s: 41 lakṣmīnivāsasthānāni viṣṇuvallakṣmyā vyāpakatā svāyambhuvādyantare bhṛgvāditastasyā utpattiśca
1.191.d: 41 लक्ष्मीनिवासस्थानानि विष्णुवल्लक्ष्म्या व्यापकता स्वायम्भुवाद्यन्तरे भृग्वादितस्तस्या उत्पत्तिश्च
1.191.m: 41. The dwelling places of Lakṣmī, the all-pervasiveness of Lakṣmī like that of Viṣṇu, and her birth from Bhṛgu and others in the intervals such as that of Svāyambhuva.

1.191.s: 42 viṣṇunā'dṛṣṭapūrvāṃ kāminītanuṃ nirmāya daityebhyo'mṛtakalaśamādāya prahlādāya brahmadinamitamāyuṣyaṃ vitīrya ca devebhyastasya dānaṃ devapaṃktyuṣpaviṣṭasūryarūpirāhuṇā tasya pānaṃ tatsūcitaviṣṇunā tacchira:kartenapurassaraṃ tasmai grahatvalokapūjyatvādivaradānam
1.191.d: 42 विष्णुनाऽदृष्टपूर्वां कामिनीतनुं निर्माय दैत्येभ्योऽमृतकलशमादाय प्रह्लादाय ब्रह्मदिनमितमायुष्यं वितीर्य च देवेभ्यस्तस्य दानं देवपंक्त्युष्पविष्टसूर्यरूपिराहुणा तस्य पानं तत्सूचितविष्णुना तच्छिर:कर्तेनपुरस्सरं तस्मै ग्रहत्वलोकपूज्यत्वादिवरदानम्
1.191.m: 42. Viṣṇu fashioned the body of a lovely woman never seen before, took the pitcher of nectar from the Daityas, granted Prahlāda a lifespan measured by a day of Brahmā, and gave it to the gods. When Rāhu, assuming the form of the Sun, sat in the row of gods and drank it, Viṣṇu, informed of this, first cut off his head, and then granted him boons such as becoming a planet and being worthy of worship by the world.
43. The defeat of the Daityas, who were enraged by Viṣṇu's decapitation of Rāhu, in battle with the gods.

1.191.s: 44 viṣṇunā yuddhe hate nidhanamāpyāpi svargarājye susiddha evaiti niścityāgrajarāhumatamanādṛtya sālvasya yuddhasthirīkaraṇam .
1.191.d: 44 विष्णुना युद्धे हते निधनमाप्यापि स्वर्गराज्ये सुसिद्ध एवैति निश्चित्याग्रजराहुमतमनादृत्य साल्वस्य युद्धस्थिरीकरणम् ।
1.191.m: 44. Sālva's determination to fight, disregarding the opinion of his elder brother Rāhu, having resolved: 'Even if I meet my death being slain by Viṣṇu in battle, [my place] in the kingdom of heaven is indeed well assured.'

1.191.s: 45 paraśurāmeṇa yuddhayārthaṃ sālvasamīpe akṛtavraṇasya preṣaṇaṃ, nāhaṃ rāmeṇa yotsye kintu tadguruśaṃkareṇa samprahariṣya ityakṛtavraṇaṃ visṛjya sālvasya yuddhārthaṃ prayāṇamū
1.191.d: 45 परशुरामेण युद्धयार्थं साल्वसमीपे अकृतव्रणस्य प्रेषणं, नाहं रामेण योत्स्ये किन्तु तद्गुरुशंकरेण सम्प्रहरिष्य इत्यकृतव्रणं विसृज्य साल्वस्य युद्धार्थं प्रयाणमू
1.191.m: 45. Paraśurāma sent Akṛtavraṇa to Sālva for the purpose of battle. Saying, 'I will not fight with Rāma, but I will strike his guru Śaṃkara,' Sālva dismissed Akṛtavraṇa and set forth for battle.
46. Description of ill omens during the march of Sālva's army...
47. The arrival of the Bhārgava on the battlefield...
48. The slaughter of Sālva's countless army by Rāma with a single fall of his battle-axe in the fight.

1.191.s: 49 paraśurāmakṛtasālvavadhatuṣṭamahendrapramukhadevānāṃ raṇabhūmāvāgatya paraśurāmakarmapraśaṃsanaṃ śaṃkareṇa tadgātrasammārjanapūrvamanuttamaśastragrāmasya pradānamarātiṃ hatvā paraśoḥ punastaddhastagamanasya ca
1.191.d: 49 परशुरामकृतसाल्ववधतुष्टमहेन्द्रप्रमुखदेवानां रणभूमावागत्य परशुरामकर्मप्रशंसनं शंकरेण तद्गात्रसम्मार्जनपूर्वमनुत्तमशस्त्रग्रामस्य प्रदानमरातिं हत्वा परशोः पुनस्तद्धस्तगमनस्य च
1.191.m: 49. The gods, headed by Mahendra, pleased with the slaying of Sālva accomplished by Paraśurāma, came to the battlefield and praised Paraśurāma's deed; and Śaṃkara, having wiped his limbs, bestowed upon him a host of unsurpassed weapons, and [granted] that his battle-axe, having slain the enemy, would return again to his hand.
50. Śaṃkara bestowed many divine missiles on Rāma, along with their secret methods of discharge and withdrawal, beginning with the gift of the Brahmā, Vaiṣṇava, Raudra, and Āgneya missiles.

1.191.s: 51 sarvadevavariṣṭho'pi bhavāṃścetasi kaṃ smaratīti śaṃkaraṃ prati paraśurāmapraśnaḥ
1.191.d: 51 सर्वदेववरिष्ठोऽपि भवांश्चेतसि कं स्मरतीति शंकरं प्रति परशुरामप्रश्नः
1.191.m: 51. Paraśurāma's question to Śaṃkara: 'Though you are the foremost among all the gods, whom do you remember in your heart?'
Now begins the Śaṃkaragītā.
52. Indication of the object of meditation in the Śaṃkaragītā...

1.191.s: 53 prajāpatiḥ kaśyapasyāditidityorbhāryayoḥ śakrahiraṇyākṣaputrayoḥ svargapātālarājye pradattavān,ekadā giriṣūtpatiteṣu dharācalanātpātāle'rṇavajalamagne devakṛtopadravaṃ śaṃkamāno hiraṇyākṣaḥ śakraṃ vijitya svārājyaṃ lebhe, hṛtasvargatridaśaprārthanayā viṣṇurnṛvarāhavapuṣānekadaityasahita hiraṇyākṣaṃ hatvā śakrāya tallokamarpitavān sa ca parvatapakṣām̐ścakarta ....
1.191.d: 53 प्रजापतिः कश्यपस्यादितिदित्योर्भार्ययोः शक्रहिरण्याक्षपुत्रयोः स्वर्गपातालराज्ये प्रदत्तवान्,एकदा गिरिषूत्पतितेषु धराचलनात्पातालेऽर्णवजलमग्ने देवकृतोपद्रवं शंकमानो हिरण्याक्षः शक्रं विजित्य स्वाराज्यं लेभे, हृतस्वर्गत्रिदशप्रार्थनया विष्णुर्नृवराहवपुषानेकदैत्यसहित हिरण्याक्षं हत्वा शक्राय तल्लोकमर्पितवान् स च पर्वतपक्षाम्̐श्चकर्त ॥॥
1.191.m: 53. The Prajāpati Kaśyapa gave the kingdoms of heaven and the nether world to Śakra and Hiraṇyākṣa, his sons by his two wives Aditi and Diti. Once, when the mountains flew up and the nether world was submerged in the waters of the ocean due to the shaking of the earth, Hiraṇyākṣa, suspecting an affliction caused by the gods, conquered Śakra and obtained sovereignty over heaven. At the entreaty of the thirty gods who were deprived of heaven, Viṣṇu, in the form of a man-boar, slew Hiraṇyākṣa along with many Daityas and restored that world to Śakra; and he [Śakra] cut off the wings of the mountains...

1.191.s: 54mahogratapastuṣṭaprajāpatinā hiraṇyakaśipave devatiryaṅnarādyavadhyavare datte tadadhamasvabhāvaśaṃkitadevaprārthanayā viṣṇostasya vadhe ca sūcite devapīḍanānte nṛsihavapuṣā viṣṇunā tadvadhaḥ .
1.191.d: 54महोग्रतपस्तुष्टप्रजापतिना हिरण्यकशिपवे देवतिर्यङ्नराद्यवध्यवरे दत्ते तदधमस्वभावशंकितदेवप्रार्थनया विष्णोस्तस्य वधे च सूचिते देवपीडनान्ते नृसिहवपुषा विष्णुना तद्वधः ।
1.191.m: 54. When the Prajāpati, pleased by the fierce asceticism [of Hiraṇyakaśipu], granted Hiraṇyakaśipu the boon of invulnerability to gods, beasts, men, and others, Viṣṇu, at the prayer of the gods who feared his base nature, indicated his death; and at the end of his torment of the gods, Viṣṇu slew him in the form of Narasiṃha.

1.191.s:
55 balinogratapasā prajāpateḥ surāsurāvadhyatvavare labdhe, prāptāyāśca daityaḥ rājatāyāṃ svargādindraprabhṛtidevanissārṇam, śakreṇa kaśyapabrahmabhyāṃ saha viṣṇave svaduḥkhaṃ nivedya vāmanarūpiṇā tena balimakhe tripādabhū
miprāptyā sumeruparyantaṃ pādadvayabhūmilābhādavaśiṣṭabhūmerabhāvādbalaye sutale sthānadānaṃ dvitīye manvantare śakratvaprāptiṃ sadā ca sutale svasannidhānādivarānadadāt
1.191.d:
55 बलिनोग्रतपसा प्रजापतेः सुरासुरावध्यत्ववरे लब्धे, प्राप्तायाश्च दैत्यः राजतायां स्वर्गादिन्द्रप्रभृतिदेवनिस्सार्णम्, शक्रेण कश्यपब्रह्मभ्यां सह विष्णवे स्वदुःखं निवेद्य वामनरूपिणा तेन बलिमखे त्रिपादभू
मिप्राप्त्या सुमेरुपर्यन्तं पादद्वयभूमिलाभादवशिष्टभूमेरभावाद्बलये सुतले स्थानदानं द्वितीये मन्वन्तरे शक्रत्वप्राप्तिं सदा च सुतले स्वसन्निधानादिवरानददात्
1.191.m: 55. When Bali obtained from the Prajāpati, by his fierce asceticism, the boon of invulnerability to gods and asuras, and the sovereignty of the Daityas was established, Indra and the other gods were expelled from heaven. Śakra reported his distress to Viṣṇu together with Kaśyapa and Brahmā. Viṣṇu, in the form of a dwarf, received three paces of land at Bali's sacrifice. Since he acquired land extending up to Mount Sumeru with two paces and there was no remaining land, he gave Bali an abode in Sutala, and granted boons such as his attaining the status of Śakra in the second Manu-interval and his own constant presence in Sutala.
56. Description of the divine manifestations of Viṣṇu.
57. Accomplishment of all goals through the worship of Viṣṇu.
58. Account of various acts that produce the pleasure of Keśava.
59. The fruit of observing fasts on weekdays, lunar mansions, and lunar days.
60. The fruit of fasting, giving gifts, and other rites on the twelfth day conjoined with Śravaṇa, on the lunar day touching three days, and on great full-moon days.
61. What is to be done in the morning worship (approaching the deity)...
62. The rule for gathering materials...
63. The rule for the time of sacrificial worship, and the definition of the measures of the honey-mixture and the rest...
64. Recitation of the time for scriptural study...

65. Account of the yoga of the five elements beginning with earth, mind, intellect, self, the unmanifest, and the Cosmic Person, preceded by postures such as the svastika, breath control, and contemplation of the gross earth.
Thus ends the Śaṃkaragītā.

66. At the entreaty of Śakra, Śaṃkara, for the sake of slaying the enemies of the gods dwelling in the nether world who were to be slain by a man, gave a Vaiṣṇava bow and quivers with inexhaustible arrows, and instructed that after the victory over the asuras, it should be given to Agastya for the sake of Rāma, the son of Daśaratha.

1.191.s: 67 viṣṇuśivayoḥ kaḥ śreṣṭha iti devapraśne viṣṇuśivayorabhedaprakaṭanapurassaraṃ madīyacāparatnaṃ bhārgavanandanāya ṛcīkaputrāya ṛcīkaputraḥ svaputrāya rāmāya dāsyati sa daityānhatvā tadrādyavāya so'pi varuṇāya so'rjunāya sa janakāya dāsyatīti vaiṣṇavadhanuṣaḥ sampradānavarṇanam
1.191.d: 67 विष्णुशिवयोः कः श्रेष्ठ इति देवप्रश्ने विष्णुशिवयोरभेदप्रकटनपुरस्सरं मदीयचापरत्नं भार्गवनन्दनाय ऋचीकपुत्राय ऋचीकपुत्रः स्वपुत्राय रामाय दास्यति स दैत्यान्हत्वा तद्राद्यवाय सोऽपि वरुणाय सोऽर्जुनाय स जनकाय दास्यतीति वैष्णवधनुषः सम्प्रदानवर्णनम्
1.191.m: 67. Upon the gods asking, 'Between Viṣṇu and Śiva, who is superior?', Śiva revealed the non-difference of Viṣṇu and Śiva, and described the transmission of the Vaiṣṇava bow: 'The jewel of my bow will be given to the son of Ṛcīka, the delight of the Bhārgavas; the son of Ṛcīka will give it to his own son Rāma; he, having slain the Daityas, will give it to Rādhyava; he will give it to Varuṇa; he to Arjuna; and he will give it to Janaka.'
68 Rāma's departure from Kailāsa to his father's hermitage, saluting his father and others, and seeing the city of Aśmaka, the abode of Varuṇa...

1.191.s:
69 varuṇapurasamṛddhivarṇanapurassaraṃ savigrahagaṃgādinadīsevitasya tasya rāmakartṛkavandanānantaraṃ varuṇakṛtarāmapūjā, tato mahādevasandeśaśravaṇāvasāne varuṇena daityebhyo samarāya dūtapreṣaṇam
.
70 vividhāstraśastraprahāridānavacamūvīrānnihatyāyaḥśaṅko rāmadvārā hananam
1.191.d:
69 वरुणपुरसमृद्धिवर्णनपुरस्सरं सविग्रहगंगादिनदीसेवितस्य तस्य रामकर्तृकवन्दनानन्तरं वरुणकृतरामपूजा, ततो महादेवसन्देशश्रवणावसाने वरुणेन दैत्येभ्यो समराय दूतप्रेषणम्
।
70 विविधास्त्रशस्त्रप्रहारिदानवचमूवीरान्निहत्यायःशङ्को रामद्वारा हननम्
1.191.m: 69 After describing the prosperity of Varuṇa's city, his worship of Rāma following Rāma's salutation to him who was attended by rivers such as the Gaṅgā in embodied form; then, after hearing the message of Mahādeva, Varuṇa sends a messenger to the Daityas for battle. / 70 After slaying the warriors of the Dānavas' army striking with diverse missiles and weapons, the slaying of Ayaḥśaṅka by Rāma.
71 Following the praise offered by Paraśurāma, Varuṇa says, "I will answer all the questions asked by you."
72 Description of months, years, and so on according to the motion of the planets, despite the extreme subtlety of Time which is of the nature of Rudra.

73 Description of the divisions of Time beginning with the twinkling of an eye and ending with the age, along with the lifespan of human beings, the increase and decrease of dharma, the division of the Vedas, and the lifespan of Brahmā in each respective [age]...

1.191.s: 74 purā kṛtādiyugānteṣu kṣatriyādibhirbrāhmaṇāditrivarṇādinipātane dvijarājādinirdiṣṭaviṣṇvavatārapramitiviprādidvārā tattadbrahmakṣatriyādināśapurassaraṃ pārāśaravyāsaprakāśitacaturvargapradīpabhūtamahābhāratasya vaiśampāyanena parīkṣinnṛpāyākhyānaṃ vedānvyasya pailajaiminyādiśiṣyāṇā madhyāpanaṃ vālmīkinirmitarāmākhyānaṃ viṣṇuyaśasaḥ kalkyudbhavatatkartavyādi ca.
1.191.d: 74 पुरा कृतादियुगान्तेषु क्षत्रियादिभिर्ब्राह्मणादित्रिवर्णादिनिपातने द्विजराजादिनिर्दिष्टविष्ण्ववतारप्रमितिविप्रादिद्वारा तत्तद्ब्रह्मक्षत्रियादिनाशपुरस्सरं पाराशरव्यासप्रकाशितचतुर्वर्गप्रदीपभूतमहाभारतस्य वैशम्पायनेन परीक्षिन्नृपायाख्यानं वेदान्व्यस्य पैलजैमिन्यादिशिष्याणा मध्यापनं वाल्मीकिनिर्मितरामाख्यानं विष्णुयशसः कल्क्युद्भवतत्कर्तव्यादि च।
1.191.m: 74 In ancient times at the ends of the Kṛta and other ages, when the three classes beginning with the brahmins were brought low by the kṣatriyas and others, the destruction of those various brahmins, kṣatriyas, and others through the avatars of Viṣṇu indicated by the lord of the twice-born and others; the narration of the Mahābhārata, the lamp of the four aims of life revealed by Vyāsa, son of Parāśara, by Vaiśampāyana to King Parīkṣit; the division of the Vedas and teaching them to disciples such as Paila and Jaimini; the story of Rāma composed by Vālmīki; and the origin of Kalki from Viṣṇuyaśas, his duties, and so on.

1.191.s:
75 kṣīṇe manvantare manvantareśvarāṇāṃ maharloke manuśakradevasaptarṣīṇāṃ brahmaloke nivāsaḥ, kulaparvatavarjyaṃ bhūlokasya nāśaḥ, naukārūpeṇa dharitryāḥ sarvabījarakṣaṇaṃ bhaviṣyanmanunā saha saptarṣīṇāṃ tatra nivāsaḥ, .
matsyarūpiśṛṃgiviṣṇornaukārakṣaṇaṃ munīnāṃ tatstavanaṃ nāvi himaśiśikharaṃ nītāyāṃ viṣṇorantardhānaṃ kṛtayugaprādurbhāvaśca.
1.191.d:
75 क्षीणे मन्वन्तरे मन्वन्तरेश्वराणां महर्लोके मनुशक्रदेवसप्तर्षीणां ब्रह्मलोके निवासः, कुलपर्वतवर्ज्यं भूलोकस्य नाशः, नौकारूपेण धरित्र्याः सर्वबीजरक्षणं भविष्यन्मनुना सह सप्तर्षीणां तत्र निवासः, ।
मत्स्यरूपिशृंगिविष्णोर्नौकारक्षणं मुनीनां तत्स्तवनं नावि हिमशिशिखरं नीतायां विष्णोरन्तर्धानं कृतयुगप्रादुर्भावश्च।
1.191.m: 75 When a manvantara has waned, the lords of the manvantara dwell in Maharloka, and the Manu, Śakra, the gods, and the seven seers dwell in Brahmaloka; the destruction of the earthly world except for the principal mountain ranges; the preservation of all seeds by the earth in the form of a boat, the dwelling there of the seven seers together with the future Manu; / the preservation of the boat by Viṣṇu with a horn in the form of a fish, the seers' praise of him, the disappearance of Viṣṇu when the boat is led to the peak of the Himalayas, and the manifestation of the Kṛta age.

1.191.s: 76 jalaprāyabhūtale saptasūryadagdhajīvānāṃ janaloke sthitiḥ, raudratejasā'rka nāśe mahāraudraghanāvāripūrṇajagati svaśarīre vāyuṣmādāya yugasahasraparyantamarṇave pitāmahaḥ svapiti vibuddhaśca sṛjati jagaditi pratikalpakramaḥ ... ...
1.191.d: 76 जलप्रायभूतले सप्तसूर्यदग्धजीवानां जनलोके स्थितिः, रौद्रतेजसाऽर्क नाशे महारौद्रघनावारिपूर्णजगति स्वशरीरे वायुष्मादाय युगसहस्रपर्यन्तमर्णवे पितामहः स्वपिति विबुद्धश्च सृजति जगदिति प्रतिकल्पक्रमः ॥॥॥
1.191.m: 76 On the earth which is mostly water, the living beings burnt by the seven suns abide in Janaloka; when the sun is destroyed by the fiery energy of Rudra, the world being filled with the waters of the terrible clouds of Rudra, the Grandfather gathers the breath into his own body and sleeps in the ocean for a thousand ages, and on waking creates the world: such is the order of every aeon...
77 Description of the unstable state of the world at the end of the aeon.

1.191.s: 78 ekārṇave bhūmitale vaṭaśākhini paryaṃṅkasthabhagavadudare brahmā trilokīdarśanāntaraṃ yugasahasramuṣitvāpyantaṃ nāpa.
1.191.d: 78 एकार्णवे भूमितले वटशाखिनि पर्यंङ्कस्थभगवदुदरे ब्रह्मा त्रिलोकीदर्शनान्तरं युगसहस्रमुषित्वाप्यन्तं नाप।
1.191.m: 78 In the single vast ocean on the surface of the earth, within the belly of the Lord reclining on a couch under the branch of a banyan tree, Brahmā, even after residing for a thousand ages seeing the three worlds, did not find the end.
79 At the end of the aeon, Viṣṇu in the form of a child is Aniruddha; Brahmā's emergence from his lotus-navel.

1.191.s: 80 brahmotpatimārabhya kālagatipūrvakaṃ vajraparīkṣijjanamejayācalavajrāṇāṃ bhāvyetadavanirakṣaṇamabhidhāya dhanañjayānantaraṃ rākṣasaiḥ sudharmasabhāyā himācale nayanam
1.191.d: 80 ब्रह्मोत्पतिमारभ्य कालगतिपूर्वकं वज्रपरीक्षिज्जनमेजयाचलवज्राणां भाव्येतदवनिरक्षणमभिधाय धनञ्जयानन्तरं राक्षसैः सुधर्मसभाया हिमाचले नयनम्
1.191.m: 80 Beginning from the origin of Brahmā, proceeding with the passage of time, stating the future protection of this earth by Vajra, Parīkṣit, Janamejaya, and Acalavajra, the abduction of the Sudharmā assembly to the Himālaya mountains by the rākṣasas after Dhanañjaya.
81 Stating the deities and other attributes of Time consisting of day, night, the aeon, and so forth, and describing the similarity of the manvantaras.

82 The deities of the Kṛta and other ages, the names of the sixty years, the rulers of the twelve-year cycles arising from the transit of Jupiter at that time, their fruits, the gentle years, the Bārhaspatya years, the lunar-mansion years, their fruits, the planets presiding over the years, and so on...

83 The half-years, months, planets, lunar mansions, lunar days, and karaṇas along with their deities; the method of calculating karaṇas, viṣṭi, planetary hours, kulika periods, Muhūrtas and their lords, and the greater fruit of worship performed at the proper time.
84 Description of the ascendants, their deities, horās, dreṣkāṇas, navāṃśas, lords of the zodiacal signs, and triṃśāṃśas...
85 Knowledge of the auspicious and inauspicious by means of the planets, lunar mansions, and so on.

86 Afflicted planets and lunar mansions bring affliction to their respective directions; even those destroyed, defeated in planetary war, debilitated, or situated in the ancestral house afflict their own respective directions...
87 Statement of the auspicious and inauspicious effects of the nine, six, three, and other lunar mansions relative to the moon's lunar mansion and others occupied at birth.
88 The number of stars in the lunar mansions beginning with Aśvinī, the spheres of planets and lunar mansions, and so on.

89 When the natal, action, collective, communal, destructive, consecration, and country lunar mansions are afflicted, worship of the respective planets preceded by lustrations with cow urine and other substances.
90 Description of the ritual of worship for planets and lunar mansions.
91 Description of the bath ritual for planets and lunar mansions with respective substances.

92 After previously setting forth the preparation of the ground, construction of the altar, and its consecration in the fire ritual, description of the concluding ritual consisting of the completion of the fire-offering with Vedic mantras to the lords of the great aeon and other presiding deities at the end of the oblation.
93 Having performed purification of the sacred diagram with the five products of the cow, the invocation of life, the worship of the planets, and so forth are described.

1.191.s: 94 sarvagrahayajane maṇḍalavidhiṃ vidhāya madhye sadhruvakoṣṭhakadvādaśakoṣṭhabhagaṇe prācyādito meṣādikalpatvā''kāśadhruvadigbhāgādimaṇḍaleṣu tattaddevatāmaṇḍaleṣu ca tattannyāsakaraṇam
1.191.d: 94 सर्वग्रहयजने मण्डलविधिं विधाय मध्ये सध्रुवकोष्ठकद्वादशकोष्ठभगणे प्राच्यादितो मेषादिकल्पत्वा'ऽकाशध्रुवदिग्भागादिमण्डलेषु तत्तद्देवतामण्डलेषु च तत्तन्न्यासकरणम्
1.191.m: 94 Having prescribed the diagram ritual in the worship of all planets, in the zodiac of twelve divisions having Dhruva's division in the centre, the performance of the respective ritual placements in the diagrams of the sky, Dhruva, and the directional portions beginning with the east as the Aries-cycle, and in the diagrams of the respective deities.
95 Invocation of Dhruva, the sky, Ananta, the planets, lunar mansions, and so forth.
96 Description of the anointings of the respective deities...
97 Presentation of garments of the respective colours, banners, ornaments, jewels, flowers, and so on to the planets, lunar mansions, and directional deities.
98 Incense, lamps, and so on of the respective substances for the respective deities.
99 Food offerings for the deities situated in the place of Dhruva...
100 Likewise the drink offerings.
101 Description of the oblation substances for the respective deities.
102 Oblation mantras for Dhruva, the directions, Brahmā, the planets, and the lunar mansions.
103 Direction regarding the sacrificial fees for the respective deities.
104 At the conclusion of the propitiation, the tying of the protective cord on the hand of the patron of the sacrifice by the officiating priest, and the blessing.
105 Statement of the fruit of the propitiation of the planets.

1.191.s: 106 graharkṣameḍhībhūtadhuvasthitacaturdaśatārakānāmanirdeśapūrvakaṃ śiśumāracakranibaddhatārakājñānataddarśanādimāhātmyakathanamū, auttānapādidhruvasya viṣṇurūpatā tannibaddhamarujjyotirgaṇasya bhramaṇam, tadadhaḥ krameṇasaptarṣimaṇḍala-bhacakra-śanaiścara-kuja-sūrya-śuka-budha-candrāṇāṃ sthitiḥ, prāgdakṣiṇagatijyotiścakrañca . navagrahāṇāñjanmavṛttam, tatra sūryatejo'sahamānāyāḥ saṃjñāyā manuyamayamunotpattyanucchāyātaḥ sāvarṇaśanaiścarotpattiḥ, uttarakuruṣu vaḍavārūpeṇa carantyāḥ saṃjñāyā kheḥ sakāśādāśvineyaraivantotpattiḥ,raivantapūjayā'śvasampatkathanañca
1.191.d: 106 ग्रहर्क्षमेढीभूतधुवस्थितचतुर्दशतारकानामनिर्देशपूर्वकं शिशुमारचक्रनिबद्धतारकाज्ञानतद्दर्शनादिमाहात्म्यकथनमू, औत्तानपादिध्रुवस्य विष्णुरूपता तन्निबद्धमरुज्ज्योतिर्गणस्य भ्रमणम्, तदधः क्रमेणसप्तर्षिमण्डल-भचक्र-शनैश्चर-कुज-सूर्य-शुक-बुध-चन्द्राणां स्थितिः, प्राग्दक्षिणगतिज्योतिश्चक्रञ्च । नवग्रहाणाञ्जन्मवृत्तम्, तत्र सूर्यतेजोऽसहमानायाः संज्ञाया मनुयमयमुनोत्पत्त्यनुच्छायातः सावर्णशनैश्चरोत्पत्तिः, उत्तरकुरुषु वडवारूपेण चरन्त्याः संज्ञाया खेः सकाशादाश्विनेयरैवन्तोत्पत्तिः,रैवन्तपूजयाऽश्वसम्पत्कथनञ्च
1.191.m: 106 With reference to the fourteen stars located at Dhruva, who serves as the central pivot for the planets and lunar mansions, an explanation of the knowledge of the stars bound to the celestial dolphin-wheel and the greatness of viewing it; the nature of Dhruva, the son of Uttānapāda, as an embodiment of Viṣṇu, and the revolution of the host of luminaries and winds bound to him; below him, in order, the position of the constellation of the seven seers, the zodiacal circle, Saturn, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon; and the eastward-southward motion of the wheel of luminaries; the account of the birth of the nine planets: therein, of Saṃjñā unable to endure the Sun's brilliance, the birth of Manu, Yama, and Yamunā, followed by the birth of Sāvarṇi and Saturn from Chāyā; of Saṃjñā wandering in the northern Kurus in the form of a mare, the birth of the two Aśvins and Revanta from the Sun; and statement of the acquisition of horses through the worship of Revanta.

1.191.s: 107 asurasurapitṛdvijādiśabdārthasandhyopāsanahetu manuṣyarākṣasagandharvādivividhasṛṣṭikathanapurassaraṃ svadharmasthitadvijānāṃ svargādyuttamalokavāsaḥ prajāpatyaṃguṣṭhābhyāṃ dakṣatatpatnīprādurbhāvatatprasūtivistāradakṣayajñe'nāhūtasatyanādaraprayuktatanutyāgena manuṣyo bhaveti dakṣāya śivaśāpādyākhyānam
1.191.d: 107 असुरसुरपितृद्विजादिशब्दार्थसन्ध्योपासनहेतु मनुष्यराक्षसगन्धर्वादिविविधसृष्टिकथनपुरस्सरं स्वधर्मस्थितद्विजानां स्वर्गाद्युत्तमलोकवासः प्रजापत्यंगुष्ठाभ्यां दक्षतत्पत्नीप्रादुर्भावतत्प्रसूतिविस्तारदक्षयज्ञेऽनाहूतसत्यनादरप्रयुक्ततनुत्यागेन मनुष्यो भवेति दक्षाय शिवशापाद्याख्यानम्
1.191.m: 107 The meaning of the terms asura, sura, ancestor, twice-born, and so forth; the reason for twilight worship; following the account of the diverse creations of humans, rākṣasas, gandharvas, and others, the residence of twice-borns steadfast in their own dharma in heaven and other supreme worlds; the manifestation of Dakṣa and his wife from the thumbs of the lord of creatures; the expansion of his offspring; and, on account of the casting off of her body out of disrespect for Satī when uninvited to Dakṣa's sacrifice, the curse given by Śiva to Dakṣa: "Become a human."

1.191.s: 108 dhuvavaṃśyakathane venasyātikāntamaryādatvādadharmanivārakahitopadeṣṭṛmunivacassvanādarācca devadattaprajñayā mantrapūtajalena taistasyāsubhirvirahīkaraṇam, punarmantrapūtakuśodakena tadūrumanthanānniṣādapṛthū utpedāte
1.191.d: 108 धुववंश्यकथने वेनस्यातिकान्तमर्यादत्वादधर्मनिवारकहितोपदेष्टृमुनिवचस्स्वनादराच्च देवदत्तप्रज्ञया मन्त्रपूतजलेन तैस्तस्यासुभिर्विरहीकरणम्, पुनर्मन्त्रपूतकुशोदकेन तदूरुमन्थनान्निषादपृथू उत्पेदाते
1.191.m: 108 In the account of the lineage of Dhruva, because Vena transgressed limits and showed disrespect toward the words of the sages who prevented adharma and offered beneficial counsel, their depriving him of his life-breaths with water consecrated by mantras using intelligence bestowed by the gods; then, from the churning of his thigh with water and kuśa grass consecrated by mantras, the arising of the Niṣāda and of Pṛthu.

1.191.s: 109 brahmaviṣṇādidevakṛtapṛthurājyābhiṣeke devadattahayagajacchatracāmarādibhi statprabhāvardhanānte sūtamāgadhastavanahṛṣṭasya tasya tābhyāmanūpamāgadhagrāmadānam, vṛttyarthiprajāprārthanayā pṛthvītaḥ sasyādyānayanaṃ svāyambhuva manusomādivatsadohanātsasyasudhāpayoviṣāṣādyutpattiḥ,pitṛviraktaprajānāṃ tenānurañjanam
1.191.d: 109 ब्रह्मविष्णादिदेवकृतपृथुराज्याभिषेके देवदत्तहयगजच्छत्रचामरादिभि स्तत्प्रभावर्धनान्ते सूतमागधस्तवनहृष्टस्य तस्य ताभ्यामनूपमागधग्रामदानम्, वृत्त्यर्थिप्रजाप्रार्थनया पृथ्वीतः सस्याद्यानयनं स्वायम्भुव मनुसोमादिवत्सदोहनात्सस्यसुधापयोविषाषाद्युत्पत्तिः,पितृविरक्तप्रजानां तेनानुरञ्जनम्
1.191.m: 109 In Pṛthu's royal consecration performed by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and other gods, after the enhancement of his majesty through horses, elephants, parasols, chowries, and the like bestowed by the gods, his granting of marshland and the Magadha village to the bard and the herald, delighted by their praise; at the request of his subjects seeking livelihood, the drawing forth of grain and other produce from the earth; from the milking [of the earth] as Svāyambhuva Manu, Soma, and others [acted as calves], the emergence of grain, nectar, milk, poison, and so forth; and his winning the affection of the subjects who had become alienated under his father.

1.191.s: 110 pṛthuputraprācīnabarhitanujānāṃ daśaprācīnabarhiṣāṃ daśavarṣaparyantaṃ tapaścaraṇena vṛkṣavṛddhayā prajākṣaye sati sammilitapracetomukhasamutthāgninā drumakṣaye somarājaprārthanayā vṛkṣarājakanyāyā māriṣayā vṛkṣāṇāṃ patnītvena grahaṇe dakṣaprajāpatijanma, tataśca haraśāpāttanmānasīsṛṣṭyuparodhe vīraṇaprajāpatikanyāyāṃ vīriṇyāṃ putrasahasrotpattiḥ, nāradopadeśanaṣṭeṣu putreṣu dakṣaśāpānnāradasya kaśyapasutatvena janma, haradvārā dakṣasyāśdhamedhabhaṅgo dakṣeṇāpi yajñe śivaṃ na yakṣyantīti śāpadānaṃ dakṣaprasūtivarṇanañca
1.191.d: 110 पृथुपुत्रप्राचीनबर्हितनुजानां दशप्राचीनबर्हिषां दशवर्षपर्यन्तं तपश्चरणेन वृक्षवृद्धया प्रजाक्षये सति सम्मिलितप्रचेतोमुखसमुत्थाग्निना द्रुमक्षये सोमराजप्रार्थनया वृक्षराजकन्याया मारिषया वृक्षाणां पत्नीत्वेन ग्रहणे दक्षप्रजापतिजन्म, ततश्च हरशापात्तन्मानसीसृष्ट्युपरोधे वीरणप्रजापतिकन्यायां वीरिण्यां पुत्रसहस्रोत्पत्तिः, नारदोपदेशनष्टेषु पुत्रेषु दक्षशापान्नारदस्य कश्यपसुतत्वेन जन्म, हरद्वारा दक्षस्याश्धमेधभङ्गो दक्षेणापि यज्ञे शिवं न यक्ष्यन्तीति शापदानं दक्षप्रसूतिवर्णनञ्च
1.191.m: 110 Because the ten Prācīnabarhis sons, offspring of Pṛthu's son Prācīnabarhis, practiced austerities for ten years, there was a destruction of living beings due to the growth of trees; when the trees were being destroyed by the fire that arose from the mouths of the gathered Pracetases, upon the plea of King Soma, their taking of Māriṣā, the daughter of the king of trees, as their wife; the birth of the lord of creatures Dakṣa; then, when his mental creation was obstructed due to the curse of Hara, the birth of a thousand sons in Vīriṇī, the daughter of the lord of creatures Vīraṇa; when those sons were lost through Nārada's instruction, Nārada's birth as the son of Kaśyapa due to Dakṣa's curse; the disruption of Dakṣa's horse-sacrifice by Hara; the pronouncement of a curse by Dakṣa too, saying, "They shall not sacrifice to Śiva in the ritual"; and the description of Dakṣa's offspring.

111 The birth in the Vaivasvata interval of the sages who were cursed by Śiva in the Svāyambhuva interval; the origin, the number of pravaras, and the prohibition of intermarriage among the sages beginning with Bhṛgu and Aṅgiras.
112 The description of the lineage of Aṅgiras and the prohibition of intermarriage among the members of his lineage.
113 Following the specification of the sage-branches that founded clans descended from Atri, the description of the sons of Atri's daughter and their mutual prohibition of intermarriage.

1.191.s: 114 atreraparavaṃśavarṇane tapasā viśvāmitrasya brāhmaṇyamāptistripravarāṇāṃ tadvaṃśyānāṃ mitho'vivāhyatā ca ..
1.191.d: 114 अत्रेरपरवंशवर्णने तपसा विश्वामित्रस्य ब्राह्मण्यमाप्तिस्त्रिप्रवराणां तद्वंश्यानां मिथोऽविवाह्यता च ॥
1.191.m: 114 In the description of the other lineage of Atri, Viśvāmitra's attainment of brahminhood through austerity, and the mutual prohibition of intermarriage among his descendants who have three pravaras.

115 In the family of Kaśyapa, son of Marīci, the description of the names of the clan-founding sages, the number of their pravaras, the clans of double descent, and so forth. 116 The description of the single-seer pravaras and others belonging to the lineage of Vasiṣṭha.

1.191.s: 117 nimipūrvapurohitavaśiṣṭhe tasyānavaratayājanaśrānte kiñcidviśramya yājayiṣya ityuttavatyapi dharmācaraṇe kālayāpanaṃ na śreya iti dvitīyapurohitadvārā yiyakṣamāṇaṃ videho bhaveti nirmi śaśāpa vaśiṣṭhaḥ; nimirapyanucitakāriṇaṃ taṃ videho bhaveti śaśāpa, brahmavaradānānmanuṣyapakṣmasu nimervāsaḥ, vaśiṣṭhajīvasya mitrāvaruṇaputratā, nāradabhaginyā'rundhatyā vaśiṣṭhasyodvāhaḥ, tasyāṃ śakterjanma, tatsutaḥ parāśaraḥ; tatputro dvaipāyanaḥ, tasya kṛṣṇanīlaraktaśvetagauradhūmraparāśarāsteṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ tryārṣeyāḥ pravarāḥ ( parāśaraśaktivaśiṣṭhāḥ ) teṣāṃ mitho'vaivāhyam ....
1.191.d: 117 निमिपूर्वपुरोहितवशिष्ठे तस्यानवरतयाजनश्रान्ते किञ्चिद्विश्रम्य याजयिष्य इत्युत्तवत्यपि धर्माचरणे कालयापनं न श्रेय इति द्वितीयपुरोहितद्वारा यियक्षमाणं विदेहो भवेति निर्मि शशाप वशिष्ठः; निमिरप्यनुचितकारिणं तं विदेहो भवेति शशाप, ब्रह्मवरदानान्मनुष्यपक्ष्मसु निमेर्वासः, वशिष्ठजीवस्य मित्रावरुणपुत्रता, नारदभगिन्याऽरुन्धत्या वशिष्ठस्योद्वाहः, तस्यां शक्तेर्जन्म, तत्सुतः पराशरः; तत्पुत्रो द्वैपायनः, तस्य कृष्णनीलरक्तश्वेतगौरधूम्रपराशरास्तेषां सर्वेषां त्र्यार्षेयाः प्रवराः ( पराशरशक्तिवशिष्ठाः ) तेषां मिथोऽवैवाह्यम् ॥॥
1.191.m: 117 When Nimi's former family priest, Vasiṣṭha, who was exhausted from continuously performing sacrifices for him, said, "Having rested a little, I will officiate for you," Vasiṣṭha cursed Nimi, who was seeking to sacrifice through a second family priest because delaying the performance of dharma is not beneficial: "Become bodiless"; Nimi too cursed him who had acted improperly: "Become bodiless"; by the boon of Brahmā, Nimi's residence in the eyelashes of human beings; the soul of Vasiṣṭha becoming the son of Mitra and Varuṇa; Vasiṣṭha's marriage to Arundhatī, the sister of Nārada; the birth of Śakti in her; his son Parāśara; his son Dvaipāyana; his [clans], the black, blue, red, white, fair, and smoky Parāśaras; all of them have three-seer pravaras (Parāśara, Śakti, and Vasiṣṭha); their mutual prohibition of intermarriage.
118 In the context of stating the lineage and pravaras of Agastya, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, and Agastya belonging to a single lineage.
119 The description of the offspring of Arundhatī.
120 The description of Kaśyapa's lineage; the birth of the Ādityas.

1.191.s: 121 hiraṇyākṣādīnnṛvarāhadirūpeṇa hatvā baliñca chalayitvā bāṇāsurayuddhe sakārtikeyarudraṃ kṛṣṇo vijigye .
1.191.d: 121 हिरण्याक्षादीन्नृवराहदिरूपेण हत्वा बलिञ्च छलयित्वा बाणासुरयुद्धे सकार्तिकेयरुद्रं कृष्णो विजिग्ये ।
1.191.m: 121 Having slain Hiraṇyākṣa and others in the form of the man-boar and other [avatāras], and having deceived Bali, Kṛṣṇa conquered Rudra along with Kārttikeya in the battle with the asura Bāṇa.
122 When the gods, defeated by the daityas led by Maya and Tāra, approached the preceptor of the gods, the removal [of the daityas] by Fire, pleased by the hymn to Agni composed by him.
123 The hymn to Vāyu composed by the preceptor of the gods to assist Agni.

1.191.s: 124 agnivāyuparājitadaityānāṃ pātāle gamanamū, kālanemino devānparājitya trailokyeśvaratvaṃ vaiṣṇavapadecchayā viṣṇudarśanañca ...
1.191.d: 124 अग्निवायुपराजितदैत्यानां पाताले गमनमू, कालनेमिनो देवान्पराजित्य त्रैलोक्येश्वरत्वं वैष्णवपदेच्छया विष्णुदर्शनञ्च ॥।
1.191.m: 124 The going of the daityas, defeated by Agni and Vāyu, to the netherworld; Kālanemi's defeat of the gods, his sovereignty over the three worlds, and his vision of Viṣṇu out of a desire for the abode of Viṣṇu.

1.191.s: 125 kālanemiṃ nipātya brahmastuto viṣṇurlokapālānyathāpurā tattatsthāneṣu yojayitvā devānyajñabhujaścakāra .
1.191.d: 125 कालनेमिं निपात्य ब्रह्मस्तुतो विष्णुर्लोकपालान्यथापुरा तत्तत्स्थानेषु योजयित्वा देवान्यज्ञभुजश्चकार ।
1.191.m: 125 Having struck down Kālanemi, Viṣṇu, praised by Brahmā, appointed the guardians of the worlds to their respective posts as before and made the gods partakers of the sacrifice.

1.191.s: 126 balibandhanakruddhadaityatāḍitabhūsuratyaktayajñe bhūtale bubhukṣitadevapreritabrahmaprārthitavarāhurūpiviṣṇunā dhvastaduṣṭadaitye pātāle kṛte sati sa hariḥ svabhaktaprahlādāyābhūtasaṃplavamāyurdaityarājatāṃ tatputravirocanāya kalpāyuṣṭvaṃ pradāya baleḥ sāvarṇikamanvantare śakratvaṃ svīkṛtya tatputraṃ bāṇaṃ svavipriyakāriṇamapi nāsubhirviyokṣya ityanucakampe
1.191.d: 126 बलिबन्धनक्रुद्धदैत्यताडितभूसुरत्यक्तयज्ञे भूतले बुभुक्षितदेवप्रेरितब्रह्मप्रार्थितवराहुरूपिविष्णुना ध्वस्तदुष्टदैत्ये पाताले कृते सति स हरिः स्वभक्तप्रह्लादायाभूतसंप्लवमायुर्दैत्यराजतां तत्पुत्रविरोचनाय कल्पायुष्ट्वं प्रदाय बलेः सावर्णिकमन्वन्तरे शक्रत्वं स्वीकृत्य तत्पुत्रं बाणं स्वविप्रियकारिणमपि नासुभिर्वियोक्ष्य इत्यनुचकम्पे
1.191.m: 126 When the brahmins on earth, beaten by the daityas who were enraged at the binding of Bali, had abandoned the sacrifice, and the evil daityas had been driven into the netherworld by Viṣṇu in the form of a boar, entreated by Brahmā who was urged by the hungry gods, that Hari, having granted an lifespan lasting until the cosmic dissolution and the kingship of the daityas to his devotee Prahlāda, and a lifespan of an aeon to his son Virocana, and having accepted Indrahood for Bali in the Sāvarṇika manvantara, felt compassion for his son Bāṇa, thinking: "Though he has acted against my wishes, I shall not deprive him of his life-breaths."

1.191.s: 127 śakrahantāraṃ putraṃ me prayaccheti ditiprārthitaḥ kaśyapo rajanīṃ tayā sahoṣitvā śucitayā varṣasahasraṃ sthāsyasi cedevaṃ bhaviṣyatītyuktvā tapase jagāma, śakrastu tāṃ chalayitvā sevitumājagāma, abdaśeṣe kāle divā suptāyāstasyā udaraṃ praviśya vajreṇa saptadhā garbhaṃ vidārya punaḥ saptadhā kṛtvonapaṃcāśanmaruto nirmitavān, ditiprārthanayā teṣāṃ sthānāni nāmāni ca cakre
1.191.d: 127 शक्रहन्तारं पुत्रं मे प्रयच्छेति दितिप्रार्थितः कश्यपो रजनीं तया सहोषित्वा शुचितया वर्षसहस्रं स्थास्यसि चेदेवं भविष्यतीत्युक्त्वा तपसे जगाम, शक्रस्तु तां छलयित्वा सेवितुमाजगाम, अब्दशेषे काले दिवा सुप्तायास्तस्या उदरं प्रविश्य वज्रेण सप्तधा गर्भं विदार्य पुनः सप्तधा कृत्वोनपंचाशन्मरुतो निर्मितवान्, दितिप्रार्थनया तेषां स्थानानि नामानि च चक्रे
1.191.m: 127 Entreated by Diti, "Grant me a son who will slay Śakra," Kaśyapa, having dwelt with her for a night, said, "If you remain in purity for a thousand years, it will be so," and went away for austerities; Śakra, however, came to serve her with deception; when a year remained, entering the belly of her who was asleep during the day, he cleaved the fetus into seven parts with his thunderbolt and then made each into seven parts, producing the forty-nine Maruts; at Diti's request, he assigned their abodes and names.

1.191.s: 128 danusiṃhikāprajotpattiprasaṃge gandharvāpsarasāṃ nāmāni tajjanma kadrū santatiḥ, ahalyānirmāṇaṃ tatkāmukaśakrasya nirvṛṣaṇatādi ca
1.191.d: 128 दनुसिंहिकाप्रजोत्पत्तिप्रसंगे गन्धर्वाप्सरसां नामानि तज्जन्म कद्रू सन्ततिः, अहल्यानिर्माणं तत्कामुकशक्रस्य निर्वृषणतादि च
1.191.m: 128 In the context of the emergence of the offspring of Danu and Siṃhikā, the names and birth of the gandharvas and apsarases; the offspring of Kadrū; the creation of Ahalyā; and the castration and other fates of Śakra who desired her.

1.191.s: 129 badaryām̐ tapasyantau naranārāyaṇau pralobhayitumāgatā daśa mauneyāpsaraso lajjayituṃ nārāyaṇena svorvoradbhutarūpasaundaryaśālinanyurvaśī nirmame
1.191.d: 129 बदर्याम्̐ तपस्यन्तौ नरनारायणौ प्रलोभयितुमागता दश मौनेयाप्सरसो लज्जयितुं नारायणेन स्वोर्वोरद्भुतरूपसौन्दर्यशालिनन्युर्वशी निर्ममे
1.191.m: 129 In order to put to shame the ten Mauneya apsarases who had come to tempt Nara and Nārāyaṇa as they practiced austerities at Badarī, Nārāyaṇa created Urvaśī from his own thighs, endowed with marvelous form and beauty.

1.191.s: 130 vaivasvatasya manordvāpare yuge devāsurayuddhaprasaṃgena svargatapurūravanṛpāsaktorvaśyā raṃbhayā sakhyā saha saṃvādaḥ
1.191.d: 130 वैवस्वतस्य मनोर्द्वापरे युगे देवासुरयुद्धप्रसंगेन स्वर्गतपुरूरवनृपासक्तोर्वश्या रंभया सख्या सह संवादः
1.191.m: 130 In the Dvāpara age of Vaivasvata Manu, in the context of the war between gods and asuras, the dialogue of Urvaśī, who was in love with King Purūravas who had gone to heaven, with her friend Rambhā.

1.191.s: 131 rambhayā sahorveśyā ākāśamārgeṇa pratiṣṭhānapurārthagamane nāradadarśanaṃ, tena ca purūravaso gṛhe vāse urvaśīputrīkṛtameṣadvayasya sadā śayanāgāre sthāpanaṃ, ghṛtamātrāhāreṇa vartanaṃ, kadācidapi nagnasya rājño'navalokanamakāmāyāstasyāḥ purūravasā ratyakaraṇam, samayeṣveṣu kasyāpi bhaṃge urvaśyāḥ śilābhāvaḥ, sarvapratijñāhāniśceti, pratiṣṭhānapurasamṛddhivarṇanam 132 kiñcidavaśiṣṭadivasabhāgaṃ yāpayituṃ rambhorvaśīṃ purūravasa ākrīḍaśobhāvarṇanamiṣeṇa vinodayāmāsa
1.191.d: 131 रम्भया सहोर्वेश्या आकाशमार्गेण प्रतिष्ठानपुरार्थगमने नारददर्शनं, तेन च पुरूरवसो गृहे वासे उर्वशीपुत्रीकृतमेषद्वयस्य सदा शयनागारे स्थापनं, घृतमात्राहारेण वर्तनं, कदाचिदपि नग्नस्य राज्ञोऽनवलोकनमकामायास्तस्याः पुरूरवसा रत्यकरणम्, समयेष्वेषु कस्यापि भंगे उर्वश्याः शिलाभावः, सर्वप्रतिज्ञाहानिश्चेति, प्रतिष्ठानपुरसमृद्धिवर्णनम् 132 किञ्चिदवशिष्टदिवसभागं यापयितुं रम्भोर्वशीं पुरूरवस आक्रीडशोभावर्णनमिषेण विनोदयामास
1.191.m: 131 When Urvaśī, accompanied by Rambhā, set out through the sky toward the city of Pratiṣṭhāna, her meeting with Nārada, who laid down the conditions: that the two rams she treated as sons must always remain in her bedchamber while dwelling in Purūravas's palace; that she would live on a diet of ghee alone; that she should never see the king naked; that Purūravas must not make love to her when she was unwilling; that upon the breach of any of these conditions Urvaśī would turn into stone and all agreements would be ruined; and a description of the opulence of the city of Pratiṣṭhāna. 132 To pass the little that remained of the day, Rambhā entertained Urvaśī on the pretext of describing the beauty of Purūravas's pleasure-garden.

1.191.s: 133 candrodaye candrakāntagṛhe sakhisahāye purūravasyāgate rambhayā nṛpasākṣātkārānantaraṃ nāradapratijñāśrāvaṇaṃ putrīkṛtameṣayorarpaṇañca, rambhāśrāvitanāradasamayasya rājñāṃgīkaraṇe prasannarambhāyai rājño ratnārpaṇaṃ tasyāśca laṃkāyāṃ dhanadātmajasya nalakūbarasya svabhartuḥ savidhaṃ gamanaṃ purūravasaścorvaśyā saha ramaṇam
1.191.d: 133 चन्द्रोदये चन्द्रकान्तगृहे सखिसहाये पुरूरवस्यागते रम्भया नृपसाक्षात्कारानन्तरं नारदप्रतिज्ञाश्रावणं पुत्रीकृतमेषयोरर्पणञ्च, रम्भाश्रावितनारदसमयस्य राज्ञांगीकरणे प्रसन्नरम्भायै राज्ञो रत्नार्पणं तस्याश्च लंकायां धनदात्मजस्य नलकूबरस्य स्वभर्तुः सविधं गमनं पुरूरवसश्चोर्वश्या सह रमणम्
1.191.m: 133 At moonrise, when Purūravas arrived at the moonstone palace accompanied by his friends, Rambhā, after meeting the king, communicated Nārada's stipulations and handed over the two rams treated as sons; when the king accepted the conditions of Nārada announced by Rambhā, he presented jewels to the pleased Rambhā, who then departed to Laṅkā to her husband Nalakūbara, son of Dhanada, while Purūravas made love with Urvaśī.

134 Description of the sports of Urvaśī and Purūravas in delightful places such as wondrous palaces, jeweled mansions, and riverbanks; the birth of their five sons headed by Āyu; and the consultation among the Gandharvas to fetch Urvaśī back.

1.191.s: 135 ugrasenagandharveṇa rātrāvurvaśīmeṣayorharaṇe tadanveṣaṇāya nagne purūravasi ca nirgate rājñaḥ pratijñābhaṅgādurvaśītirodhāne rājñaḥ pralāpaḥ
1.191.d: 135 उग्रसेनगन्धर्वेण रात्रावुर्वशीमेषयोर्हरणे तदन्वेषणाय नग्ने पुरूरवसि च निर्गते राज्ञः प्रतिज्ञाभङ्गादुर्वशीतिरोधाने राज्ञः प्रलापः
1.191.m: 135 When the Gandharva Ugrasena abducted Urvaśī's two rams by night and Purūravas rushed out naked to search for them, Urvaśī vanished because the king had broken the condition, whereupon the king lamented.

1.191.s: 136 purūravovirahasantaptāyā urvaśyā nāradopadeśādekarātraṃ sahavāsaḥ, gamanasamaye ca gandharvopāsanayā matsaṅgamo bhaviṣyatītyurvaśyupadeśādrājña ekavatsaraparyantaṃ ghoratapaścaraṇaṃ nāradaṃ puraskṛtya gandharvāṇāṃ tatra gatvā varadānānte gandharvatvakārakayāvanmanvantaraṃ tayā saha krīḍākaraṇasya tadanu ca candramaḥpraveśapitṛlokaprāpteśca vare prāpya sabālasya purūravasa urvaśīdattasasthālīkaviśvāyunāmakabālakasya svapure nayanam, mārge gandharvaiḥ sthālyāharaṇaṃ paścācchamīgarbhādagnyutpādanādyupadeśaṃ kṛtvā rājño gandharvatvakārakopadeśaḥ 137 aśvamedhavājapeyāgniṣṭomātirātrādiyajñakaraṇapūrvakaṃ rājño dharitryāmekarāṣṭratvaṃ prajānāmatīva saukhyaṃ rājye dharmaprādhānyatādyupabhujya rājño dehasahitaṃ tridivagamanam
1.191.d: 136 पुरूरवोविरहसन्तप्ताया उर्वश्या नारदोपदेशादेकरात्रं सहवासः, गमनसमये च गन्धर्वोपासनया मत्सङ्गमो भविष्यतीत्युर्वश्युपदेशाद्राज्ञ एकवत्सरपर्यन्तं घोरतपश्चरणं नारदं पुरस्कृत्य गन्धर्वाणां तत्र गत्वा वरदानान्ते गन्धर्वत्वकारकयावन्मन्वन्तरं तया सह क्रीडाकरणस्य तदनु च चन्द्रमःप्रवेशपितृलोकप्राप्तेश्च वरे प्राप्य सबालस्य पुरूरवस उर्वशीदत्तसस्थालीकविश्वायुनामकबालकस्य स्वपुरे नयनम्, मार्गे गन्धर्वैः स्थाल्याहरणं पश्चाच्छमीगर्भादग्न्युत्पादनाद्युपदेशं कृत्वा राज्ञो गन्धर्वत्वकारकोपदेशः 137 अश्वमेधवाजपेयाग्निष्टोमातिरात्रादियज्ञकरणपूर्वकं राज्ञो धरित्र्यामेकराष्ट्रत्वं प्रजानामतीव सौख्यं राज्ये धर्मप्राधान्यताद्युपभुज्य राज्ञो देहसहितं त्रिदिवगमनम्
1.191.m: 136 By the counsel of Nārada, Urvaśī, who was distressed by separation from Purūravas, dwelled with him for one night, and at the time of her departure she instructed the king, 'You shall be reunited with me through worship of the Gandharvas'; after the king performed severe austerities for an entire year, he approached the Gandharvas led by Nārada, and after granting him boons—conferring the status of a Gandharva, sporting with her for the duration of a manvantara, and thereafter entering the moon and attaining the world of the ancestors—Purūravas took his young son named Viśvāyu, born of Urvaśī, along with a vessel given by her, and led him to his own city; on the way, the Gandharvas took back the vessel, but afterward instructed him on producing fire from the hollow of a śamī tree and gave the king the teachings that confer the status of a Gandharva. 137 Having performed sacrifices such as the horse sacrifice, the Vājapeya, the Agniṣṭoma, and the Atirātra, the king established sole dominion over the earth, the subjects enjoyed utmost happiness, dharma was preeminent in the kingdom, and, having experienced all this, the king ascended to heaven in his physical body.
138 The innumerable hosts of ancestors, both embodied and bodiless; the satisfaction of the ancestors for one who offers a śrāddha, his prosperity, and so forth.

1.191.s: 139 hiraṇyākṣavadhānantaraṃ saukaravapuṣā rasātalādvasudhāmānīya daṃṣṭrāgralagnaṃ mṛtpiṇḍaṃ dakṣiṇe kare kṛtvā svaprasvedaromabhyāṃ tiladarbhau nirmāya viṣṇoḥ piṇḍadāna (śrāddha ) maryādāprakaṭanam
1.191.d: 139 हिरण्याक्षवधानन्तरं सौकरवपुषा रसातलाद्वसुधामानीय दंष्ट्राग्रलग्नं मृत्पिण्डं दक्षिणे करे कृत्वा स्वप्रस्वेदरोमभ्यां तिलदर्भौ निर्माय विष्णोः पिण्डदान (श्राद्ध ) मर्यादाप्रकटनम्
1.191.m: 139 After slaying Hiraṇyākṣa and bringing the earth up from the nether world in the form of a boar, [Viṣṇu] placed the lump of earth clinging to the tip of his tusk upon his right hand, produced sesame seeds and darbha grass from his own sweat and body-hair, and established the proper rule of the offering of funeral cakes (śrāddha).

140 Having worshipped Viṣṇu as the Boar on the day of the śrāddha, one who maintains the sacred fires or one who does not, according to his qualification, carries out the invocation of suitable twice-born ancestors, their worship, the scattering of funeral cakes, their adoration, the offering of milk-rice and other foods, the prayer for imperishable giving, and so forth; and the declaration of the Seven Sages' mantra as well as the qualification of the performer of the śrāddha.
141 The proper places for a śrāddha, and the deliberation on what should and should not be offered there.
142 The varieties of śrāddha, and their results at ordinary and special times.
143 Deliberation on worthy and unworthy recipients at a śrāddha.
144 Recitation of the places for śrāddha, such as the Gaṅgā, the Yamunā, Sannihatyā, sacred forests, and so forth.
145 The fruit of observing the vow and performing a śrāddha on the Aśūnyaśayanadvitīyā.

1.191.s: 146 avidyāvihitakarmaṇā saṃsāraṃ vidyāvihitasya ca tasya mokṣasādhanatāmuktvā pāṇḍavānāṃ kṛṣṇasācivyādbhāgyavattaratādikathanapurassaraṃ dharmarūpavṛṣalakṣaṇavarṇanam
1.191.d: 146 अविद्याविहितकर्मणा संसारं विद्याविहितस्य च तस्य मोक्षसाधनतामुक्त्वा पाण्डवानां कृष्णसाचिव्याद्भाग्यवत्तरतादिकथनपुरस्सरं धर्मरूपवृषलक्षणवर्णनम्
1.191.m: 146 Having explained that rites performed in ignorance lead to worldly existence, whereas those performed with spiritual knowledge serve as the means to liberation, and having proclaimed the superior fortune of the Pāṇḍavas on account of Kṛṣṇa's assistance, description of the marks of the bull that is the embodiment of dharma.
147 The time, fruit, duties, and so forth concerning the release of a bull […].
148 Description of the deeds of Purūravas in his previous life […].
149 Description of the beauty of the Irāvatī river situated on the Himavat mountain.
150 Description of the Himavat.

151 The king's entrance into the hermitage of Atri, which was adorned with rows of many trees and creepers possessing an abundance of delightful blossoms and fruits, made resonant with the sweet murmurs of various flocks of birds, adorned with many kinds of wild beasts that had abandoned their innate hostility, and which brought joy to the king upon beholding rocks that flowed with curd and milk.

1.191.s: 152 añyāśramasarasi tatsiddhisañjātasauvarṇarājatavaidrumādiviṭapiśobhitavedikāyāṃ padmarāgacchadavatpadmaśobhādiyutāyāṃ vividharatnasanāthabhūmyāṃ tādṛśe ca prāsāde bhagavato janārdanasya bhogibhogāvalyāṃ śayānasya rājñā vandanam, tasyaivāśramasyaikadeśe tapaścaraṇañca
1.191.d: 152 अञ्याश्रमसरसि तत्सिद्धिसञ्जातसौवर्णराजतवैद्रुमादिविटपिशोभितवेदिकायां पद्मरागच्छदवत्पद्मशोभादियुतायां विविधरत्नसनाथभूम्यां तादृशे च प्रासादे भगवतो जनार्दनस्य भोगिभोगावल्यां शयानस्य राज्ञा वन्दनम्, तस्यैवाश्रमस्यैकदेशे तपश्चरणञ्च
1.191.m: 152 The king's homage to the Lord Janārdana lying upon the coils of the serpent in another hermitage, on a platform adorned with trees of gold, silver, coral, and other treasures produced by its spiritual power, at a lake adorned with lotuses resembling rubies, upon ground rich in various gems, and inside such a palace; and [the king's] performance of austerities in a corner of that very hermitage.

1.191.s: 153 tatrāśrame gandharvāṇāmapsarobhirvividhavihārānpaśyannapyalolo rājā mahattapaścakāra tatkarmatuṣṭagandharvebhyo madhusūdanaprasādaṃ yayāce
1.191.d: 153 तत्राश्रमे गन्धर्वाणामप्सरोभिर्विविधविहारान्पश्यन्नप्यलोलो राजा महत्तपश्चकार तत्कर्मतुष्टगन्धर्वेभ्यो मधुसूदनप्रसादं ययाचे
1.191.m: 153 In that hermitage, the king, though witnessing the varied sports of the Gandharvas with the Apsarases, remained steadfast and performed severe austerities; and from the Gandharvas who were pleased by that deed he requested the grace of Madhusūdana.

1.191.s: 154 madrarājasya ( bhāvipurūravasaḥ ) svapne'trisamāgamaḥ kṛtakṛtyatā ca bhaviṣyatīti darśanaṃ prabhāte jāgradavasthāyāmatridarśanaṃ, pūrvajanmani dvādaśīvratakaraṇādbhagavati viṣṇau prasanne tava madāśramaprāptiratra ca kṣaudrayuktaśilāprāye mākṣikādiphalayuktapradeśe niraśanapūrvakatapasā prasannena viṣṇunā bhavadicchā'moghīkriyata ityuttamarūpaprāptaye rūpasatropadeśaḥ
1.191.d: 154 मद्रराजस्य ( भाविपुरूरवसः ) स्वप्नेऽत्रिसमागमः कृतकृत्यता च भविष्यतीति दर्शनं प्रभाते जाग्रदवस्थायामत्रिदर्शनं, पूर्वजन्मनि द्वादशीव्रतकरणाद्भगवति विष्णौ प्रसन्ने तव मदाश्रमप्राप्तिरत्र च क्षौद्रयुक्तशिलाप्राये माक्षिकादिफलयुक्तप्रदेशे निरशनपूर्वकतपसा प्रसन्नेन विष्णुना भवदिच्छाऽमोघीक्रियत इत्युत्तमरूपप्राप्तये रूपसत्रोपदेशः
1.191.m: 154 The king of Madra (the future Purūravas) experienced in a dream his meeting with Atri and had the vision that he would attain his goal; in the morning, while awake, he saw Atri, who gave him the instruction on the sacrifice of beauty (rūpasatra) for the attainment of supreme beauty, saying: 'Because you observed the dvādaśī vow in your previous birth, the blessed Lord Viṣṇu was pleased and you have reached my hermitage; and here, in this region largely consisting of rocks filled with honey and possessed of honey-like fruits, Viṣṇu, pleased by your austerities accompanied by fasting, will make your desire unfailing.'
155 The performance of the sacrifice of beauty by a brahmin learned in astronomy, traditional histories, and other lores, according to the instruction of his guru, and its fruits […].

1.191.s: 156 bhagavatātriṇā madrarājasya rūpasatre gurutvamurarīkṛtya yathāvidhi tatsatrasampādanaṃ tadavasāne ca rājño'pūrvarūpasampatyā paurajānapadeṣvadhikapūjyatā, bhūyaśca dehāvasāne budhaputratā, sadehasya tasya svarloke gamanañca
1.191.d: 156 भगवतात्रिणा मद्रराजस्य रूपसत्रे गुरुत्वमुररीकृत्य यथाविधि तत्सत्रसम्पादनं तदवसाने च राज्ञोऽपूर्वरूपसम्पत्या पौरजानपदेष्वधिकपूज्यता, भूयश्च देहावसाने बुधपुत्रता, सदेहस्य तस्य स्वर्लोके गमनञ्च
1.191.m: 156 The revered Atri's accepting the role of guru in the sacrifice of beauty for the king of Madra and duly performing that sacrifice; at its conclusion, the king's receiving unprecedented beauty and thus greater reverence among the citizens and countryfolk; and further, at the end of his life, his being born as the son of Budha, and his ascending to heaven in his physical body.
157 The procedure of the vow on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa for one who desires sovereignty.
158 Description of the Kāmadvādaśī.
159 The fruits equal to sacrifices such as the Agniṣṭoma obtained by worshipping Keśava on the twelfth lunar days of the bright fortnights beginning with Mārgaśīrṣa […].
160 The procedure for the twelfth lunar days of every dark fortnight, and the fruit of performing it […].

161 The fruit of fasting on the dvādaśī conjoined with the Śravaṇa asterism in the bright fortnight of the month of Bhādrapada for those unable to fast on all dvādaśīs, and the extreme greatness of that very [day] when conjoined with Wednesday and Śravaṇa.

1.191.s: 162 śravaṇadvādaśīprasaṃgena puṇyanadīsaṃgamasnānatajjalapūrṇavāridhānyā dadhyodanasahitāyā dānasya prāśastyam . pūrvajanmani maruprāntasthaśākalanagaravāstavyasya kasyacidvaiśyasya śravaṇadvādaśyāṃ tauṣīcandrabhāgayornadyoḥ saṃgame sadadhyodanavāridhānīdānājjanmāntare pretādhipatāyāmapi nityaṃ bhojanasamaye dadhyodanayuktavāridhānyupasthitivarṇanam
1.191.d: 162 श्रवणद्वादशीप्रसंगेन पुण्यनदीसंगमस्नानतज्जलपूर्णवारिधान्या दध्योदनसहिताया दानस्य प्राशस्त्यम् । पूर्वजन्मनि मरुप्रान्तस्थशाकलनगरवास्तव्यस्य कस्यचिद्वैश्यस्य श्रवणद्वादश्यां तौषीचन्द्रभागयोर्नद्योः संगमे सदध्योदनवारिधानीदानाज्जन्मान्तरे प्रेताधिपतायामपि नित्यं भोजनसमये दध्योदनयुक्तवारिधान्युपस्थितिवर्णनम्
1.191.m: 162 In connection with Śravaṇadvādaśī, the praise of bathing at the confluence of sacred rivers and donating a water vessel filled with that water accompanied by curd-rice; the account of a certain vaiśya residing in the city of Śākala on the edge of the desert, who, having donated a water vessel along with curd-rice on Śravaṇadvādaśī at the confluence of the Tauṣī and Candrabhāgā rivers in a previous birth, had a water vessel accompanied by curd-rice appear every day at mealtime in his next birth, even though he had become a lord of the deceased.
163 The praise of sesame on Tiladvādaśī for bathing, oblation, food offerings, lamps, and gifts of water.

1.191.s: 164 māgadheṣu caṇḍavegarājamahiṣī nayanasundarī pūrvajanmani śravaṇadvādaśyāṃ tilahemadānādikāraṇādrājñītvamāpa, tatsakhīmatallikayā vāsantikayā tatkāraṇe pṛṣṭe pūrvajanmani brāhmaṇyai tasyaitaddeśasthadadhivāhanasya rājño bhāryayā kamalākhyayā sakhyavaśādumārūpavitastānadyāṃ snātvopavāsapūrvakaviṣṇupūjāhavanakarmaṇi vahnimukhabhraṣṭatilapuṇyaphaladānātsvasyā rājamahiṣītvādi nijagāda...
1.191.d: 164 मागधेषु चण्डवेगराजमहिषी नयनसुन्दरी पूर्वजन्मनि श्रवणद्वादश्यां तिलहेमदानादिकारणाद्राज्ञीत्वमाप, तत्सखीमतल्लिकया वासन्तिकया तत्कारणे पृष्टे पूर्वजन्मनि ब्राह्मण्यै तस्यैतद्देशस्थदधिवाहनस्य राज्ञो भार्यया कमलाख्यया सख्यवशादुमारूपवितस्तानद्यां स्नात्वोपवासपूर्वकविष्णुपूजाहवनकर्मणि वह्निमुखभ्रष्टतिलपुण्यफलदानात्स्वस्या राजमहिषीत्वादि निजगाद॥।
1.191.m: 164 Among the Magadhas, Queen Nayanasundarī, wife of King Caṇḍavega, attained queenship because of gifts of sesame, gold, and other things on Śravaṇadvādaśī in a previous birth; when asked about that cause by her excellent friend Vāsantikā, she recounted her status as queen and so forth, [which came about] because in a previous birth, when she was a brahmin woman, Queen Kamalā, wife of King Dadhivāhana of that country, had out of friendship bathed in the Vitastā river which has the form of Umā, fasted, worshipped Viṣṇu and offered oblations, and given [her] the meritorious fruit of the sesame seeds that had fallen from the fire's mouth...

1.191.s: 165 gāyatrīdevatāśaktipravacanaṃ tasyā gāyatrīsāvitryādyanvarthanāmanirvacana ñcābhidhāya tajjāpasya sarvārthasādhakatoṅkārasahitāyāstayāḥ paramapuruṣasahitacaturviṃśatitattvātmakatādivarṇanam ...
1.191.d: 165 गायत्रीदेवताशक्तिप्रवचनं तस्या गायत्रीसावित्र्याद्यन्वर्थनामनिर्वचन ञ्चाभिधाय तज्जापस्य सर्वार्थसाधकतोङ्कारसहितायास्तयाः परमपुरुषसहितचतुर्विंशतितत्त्वात्मकतादिवर्णनम् ॥।
1.191.m: 165 The discourse on the power of the goddess Gāyatrī; having explained the etymological definitions of her meaningful names such as Gāyatrī and Sāvitrī, the description of how reciting her [mantra] accomplishes all goals, and how along with the syllable Oṃ she consists of the twenty-four principles along with the Supreme Person, and so forth...

1.191.s: 166 dvādaśyamāvāsyādiṣu keśavādisthāneṣu dīpadānasya tathā kārtikamāsa ākāśadīpadānasya phalam
1.191.d: 166 द्वादश्यमावास्यादिषु केशवादिस्थानेषु दीपदानस्य तथा कार्तिकमास आकाशदीपदानस्य फलम्
1.191.m: 166 The fruit of offering lamps at shrines of Keśava and others on the twelfth day, the new moon day, and so forth, as well as offering an aerial lamp in the month of Kārtika.

1.191.s: 167 vidarbhādhipacitrarathatanayā lalitā triśatabhāryasyāpi kāśirājasya priyarājñītvaṃ viṣṇvāyatanādiṣu dīpadānādavāpa, sauvīrarājapurohitamaitreyeṇomārūpadevikāsarittīrthe nirmitaviṣṇvālaye kārtikamāsi dyūtasya dīpasya vartipreraṇena mṛtāyā mūṣikāyā janmāntare vidarbharājakanyātvaṃ kāśirājapriyamahiṣītvañca
1.191.d: 167 विदर्भाधिपचित्ररथतनया ललिता त्रिशतभार्यस्यापि काशिराजस्य प्रियराज्ञीत्वं विष्ण्वायतनादिषु दीपदानादवाप, सौवीरराजपुरोहितमैत्रेयेणोमारूपदेविकासरित्तीर्थे निर्मितविष्ण्वालये कार्तिकमासि द्यूतस्य दीपस्य वर्तिप्रेरणेन मृताया मूषिकाया जन्मान्तरे विदर्भराजकन्यात्वं काशिराजप्रियमहिषीत्वञ्च
1.191.m: 167 Lalitā, the daughter of Citraratha, king of Vidarbha, became the beloved queen of the king of Kāśi—even though he had three hundred wives—because of offering lamps in temples of Viṣṇu and elsewhere; a female mouse, having died in a temple of Viṣṇu constructed at the tīrtha of the Devikā river in the form of Umā by Maitreya, the family priest of the Sauvīra king, by stirring the wick of a flickering lamp in the month of Kārtika, attained the status of a Vidarbha princess and the beloved queen of the king of Kāśi in her next birth.

1.191.s: 168 upavāsāśaktadhanahīnānāmapi sarvasulabheṣu puṇyāraṇyeṣvayatnasādhyāsu ca puṣpaphalatoyādisāmagrīṣu keśavārciyā sarvakāmasamṛddhiḥ svāyattā
1.191.d: 168 उपवासाशक्तधनहीनानामपि सर्वसुलभेषु पुण्यारण्येष्वयत्नसाध्यासु च पुष्पफलतोयादिसामग्रीषु केशवार्चिया सर्वकामसमृद्धिः स्वायत्ता
1.191.m: 168 Even for those incapable of fasting and destitute of wealth, the abundance of all desires is brought under one's control through the worship of Keśava with materials easily obtained by everyone in sacred forests without effort, such as flowers, fruits, and water.
169 The rewards of one who performs sweeping and other cleaning in a temple of Viṣṇu and other places.

1.191.s: 170 kasmiśriddhatadaive śūdre vāṇijyakṛṣinaṣṭadhane gaṃgātaṭasthavarāhamaṃdiralepanādyaśakte kākatālīyavaddharāhārcādidṛkṣārthaṃ sauvīrarāja āgataḥ tatsampattilubdhacittaḥ śūdraḥ pañcatāñjagāma, tadbhāryā tena sahaikacityā bhasmasādabhavat, tatpuṇyavaśātsa svargalokaṅgataḥ tadaiva yuvanāśvo putrīyavratena viṣṇumānārca, svapne bhārgavaṃ cyavanaṃ gaccheti viṣṇavādiṣṭaḥ sa nṛpastaṃ svavṛttamavadat cyavano'pi tadajñātaṃ putrīyaṃ jalaṃ kṛtvā kalaśe sthāpayāmāsa, niśīthe rājñā tṛṣārtena tajjale pīte munyanugrahādrājñaḥ kukṣau garbhaḥ sañjātaḥ māndhāteti tannāma śūdrātmā taṃ viveśa, śūdrabhāryā kāśirājaduhitṛtāṃ yātā māndhātror̤hā udvāhānantaraṃ yuvanāśvastamayodhyāyāmabhiṣicya vanastho nākamagamat
1.191.d: 170 कस्मिश्रिद्धतदैवे शूद्रे वाणिज्यकृषिनष्टधने गंगातटस्थवराहमंदिरलेपनाद्यशक्ते काकतालीयवद्धराहार्चादिदृक्षार्थं सौवीरराज आगतः तत्सम्पत्तिलुब्धचित्तः शूद्रः पञ्चताञ्जगाम, तद्भार्या तेन सहैकचित्या भस्मसादभवत्, तत्पुण्यवशात्स स्वर्गलोकङ्गतः तदैव युवनाश्वो पुत्रीयव्रतेन विष्णुमानार्च, स्वप्ने भार्गवं च्यवनं गच्छेति विष्णवादिष्टः स नृपस्तं स्ववृत्तमवदत् च्यवनोऽपि तदज्ञातं पुत्रीयं जलं कृत्वा कलशे स्थापयामास, निशीथे राज्ञा तृषार्तेन तज्जले पीते मुन्यनुग्रहाद्राज्ञः कुक्षौ गर्भः सञ्जातः मान्धातेति तन्नाम शूद्रात्मा तं विवेश, शूद्रभार्या काशिराजदुहितृतां याता मान्धात्रोर्̤हा उद्वाहानन्तरं युवनाश्वस्तमयोध्यायामभिषिच्य वनस्थो नाकमगमत्
1.191.m: 170 When a certain ill-fated śūdra, having lost his wealth in trade and agriculture, was unable even to plaster the Varāha temple on the bank of the Gaṅgā, the Sauvīra king arrived as if by the coincidence of the crow and the palm fruit to view the image of Varāha; his mind covetous of that wealth, the śūdra met his death, and his wife was reduced to ashes on the same funeral pyre with him; by the power of that merit, he went to heaven; at that very time, Yuvanāśva worshipped Viṣṇu with a rite for obtaining a son; instructed by Viṣṇu in a dream to go to Bhārgava Cyavana, that king recounted his story to him; Cyavana, having consecrated water for obtaining a son without his knowledge, placed it in a pot; at midnight, when that water was drunk by the king who was afflicted with thirst, a child was conceived in the king's belly by the sage's grace; named Māndhātṛ, the soul of the śūdra entered him, while the śūdra's wife became the daughter of the king of Kāśi and was wedded to Māndhātṛ; after the marriage, Yuvanāśva consecrated him in Ayodhyā, went to the forest, and departed for heaven.

1.191.s:
171 māndhātari viṣṇvaṃśasya vidyamāne'pi lavaṇena māheśvaraśūlena sa kathaṃ hata iti saṃśayodbhāvanapurassaraṃ śivaviṣṇvabhedasya puruṣasvarūpasya
varṇanam
1.191.d:
171 मान्धातरि विष्ण्वंशस्य विद्यमानेऽपि लवणेन माहेश्वरशूलेन स कथं हत इति संशयोद्भावनपुरस्सरं शिवविष्ण्वभेदस्य पुरुषस्वरूपस्य
वर्णनम्
1.191.m: 171 Following the raising of a doubt as to how Māndhātṛ was killed by Lavaṇa with a spear of Maheśvara even though a portion of Viṣṇu was present [in him], the description of the non-difference between Śiva and Viṣṇu and of the nature of the Cosmic Person.

1.191.s: 172 hareḥ prādurbhāveṣu suranaratiyaktvamanāsthāyaiva jagatpālanam .. māyāleśamantareṇa yathāruci dharmarakṣāpurassaramamānavīyakarmācaraṇam .
1.191.d: 172 हरेः प्रादुर्भावेषु सुरनरतियक्त्वमनास्थायैव जगत्पालनम् ॥ मायालेशमन्तरेण यथारुचि धर्मरक्षापुरस्सरममानवीयकर्माचरणम् ।
1.191.m: 172 In the manifestations of Hari, his protection of the world without relying on being a god, man, or animal; the performance of superhuman deeds, preserving dharma according to his wish, without the slightest trickery.

1.191.s: 173 mārgaśīrṣamāsamārabhya māsanakṣatreṣūpavāsapūrvakaṃ harervāmajānvādyekaikamaṅgaṃ pūjayitvā gomūtreṇa snānaṃ raktapuṣpaiḥ pūjanaṃ tāmrasya dānamityādi krameṇa putrīyānantavratakathanam
1.191.d: 173 मार्गशीर्षमासमारभ्य मासनक्षत्रेषूपवासपूर्वकं हरेर्वामजान्वाद्येकैकमङ्गं पूजयित्वा गोमूत्रेण स्नानं रक्तपुष्पैः पूजनं ताम्रस्य दानमित्यादि क्रमेण पुत्रीयानन्तव्रतकथनम्
1.191.m: 173 The explanation of the Putrīyānantavrata in order: beginning from the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, fasting on the asterisms of each month, worshipping each limb of Hari beginning with the left knee, bathing with cow urine, worshipping with red flowers, donating copper, and so forth.
174 The procedure for worshipping on the asterisms of each month beginning from the month of Kārtika.
175 The deeds of many Śakras recounted by Śāmbarāyaṇi, and the slaying of their enemies by Viṣṇu...

176 The mention of the names of the first Manu, the mind-born son of Brahmā, his sons, the seven seers beginning with Marīci, the Viśvabhuk Indra who drinks soma with Jaya and others, and the foremost Daityas who are his enemies, such as Bāṣkala.
177 In the narrative of Śāmbarāyaṇi addressed to Śakra, the mention of the names of the descendants and others in the interval of the second Manu, Svārociṣa.

1.191.s: 178 tṛtīyasyauttamasya manorajādisaptaputtrāṇāṃ rajobāhvādisaptarcyādīnāśca kīrtanam 179 caturthasya tāmasākhyamanorjānujaṃghādiputtrāṇāṃ vanādināmakasaptarṣīṇāṃ satyādidevagaṇānāñca varṇanam
1.191.d: 178 तृतीयस्यौत्तमस्य मनोरजादिसप्तपुत्त्राणां रजोबाह्वादिसप्तर्च्यादीनाश्च कीर्तनम् 179 चतुर्थस्य तामसाख्यमनोर्जानुजंघादिपुत्त्राणां वनादिनामकसप्तर्षीणां सत्यादिदेवगणानाञ्च वर्णनम्
1.191.m: 178 The mention of the seven sons beginning with Aja, the seven seers beginning with Rajobāhu, and others, of the third Manu, Auttama. 179 The description of the sons beginning with Jānujaṅgha, the seven seers named Vana and others, and the groups of gods beginning with the Satyas, of the fourth Manu named Tāmasa.

1.191.s: 180 paṃcamasya raivatasya manormahāpurāṇādiputrāṇāṃ vedaśrutyādisaptarṣīṇāmābhūtarājasādidevagaṇānāṃ vibhorindrasya śambvākhyadaityapatyādīnāñca varṇanam
