1.191.d: 180 पंचमस्य रैवतस्य मनोर्महापुराणादिपुत्राणां वेदश्रुत्यादिसप्तर्षीणामाभूतराजसादिदेवगणानां विभोरिन्द्रस्य शम्ब्वाख्यदैत्यपत्यादीनाञ्च वर्णनम्
1.191.m: 180 The description of the sons beginning with Mahāpurāṇa, the seven seers beginning with Vedaśruti, the groups of gods beginning with the Ābhūtarajasas, the Indra named Vibhu, the Daitya lord named Śambhu, and others, of the fifth Manu, Raivata.

1.191.s: 181 ṣaṣṭhasya manoścākṣuṣasyorvādiputrāṇāmāḍhyādisaptarṣīṇāṃ divaukasāmaṣṭakādipaṃcagaṇānāṃ manojavākhyasyendrasya ca kīrtanam, daityarājasya mahāmālasya varṇanam
1.191.d: 181 षष्ठस्य मनोश्चाक्षुषस्योर्वादिपुत्राणामाढ्यादिसप्तर्षीणां दिवौकसामष्टकादिपंचगणानां मनोजवाख्यस्येन्द्रस्य च कीर्तनम्, दैत्यराजस्य महामालस्य वर्णनम्
1.191.m: 181 The mention of the sons beginning with Uru, the seven seers beginning with Āḍhya, the five groups of heaven-dwellers beginning with the Aṣṭakas, and the Indra named Manojava, of the sixth Manu, Cākṣuṣa; and the description of the Daitya king Mahāmāla.

1.191.s: 182 saptamasya vaivasvatasya manorikṣvākvādiputtrāṇām atryādisaptarṣīṇām ekonapaṃcāśadasuradevānāmāśvinādidaśānāmaparadevānāmojambināmakasya śakrasya kīrtanaṃ hiraṇyākṣasya devārāternavarāharūpeṇa viṣṇunā yā vadhādikathanañca
1.191.d: 182 सप्तमस्य वैवस्वतस्य मनोरिक्ष्वाक्वादिपुत्त्राणाम् अत्र्यादिसप्तर्षीणाम् एकोनपंचाशदसुरदेवानामाश्विनादिदशानामपरदेवानामोजम्बिनामकस्य शक्रस्य कीर्तनं हिरण्याक्षस्य देवारातेर्नवराहरूपेण विष्णुना या वधादिकथनञ्च
1.191.m: 182 The mention of the sons beginning with Ikṣvāku, the seven seers beginning with Atri, the forty-nine Asura gods, the ten other gods beginning with the Aśvins, and the Śakra named Ojambin, of the seventh Manu, Vaivasvata; and the account of the slaying of the gods' enemy Hiraṇyākṣa by Viṣṇu in the form of a new boar, and so forth.

1.191.s: 183 aṣṭamasya bhaviṣyasya sāvarṇasya manorvijayādiputrāṇāmaśvatthāmādisaptarṣīṇāṃ sutapasādidevagaṇānāṃ balerindrasya niḥsapatnasya kīrtanamra, tasminmanvantare himācalasthaṃ nānolaṃ viṣṇurhaniṣyatīti kathanañca
1.191.d: 183 अष्टमस्य भविष्यस्य सावर्णस्य मनोर्विजयादिपुत्राणामश्वत्थामादिसप्तर्षीणां सुतपसादिदेवगणानां बलेरिन्द्रस्य निःसपत्नस्य कीर्तनम्र, तस्मिन्मन्वन्तरे हिमाचलस्थं नानोलं विष्णुर्हनिष्यतीति कथनञ्च
1.191.m: 183 The mention of the sons beginning with Vijaya, the seven seers beginning with Aśvatthāman, the groups of gods beginning with the Sutapases, and Indra Bali without rivals, of the eighth, future Manu, Sāvarṇa; and the statement that in that manvantara Viṣṇu will slay Nānola residing on the Himālaya.

1.191.s: 184 brahmaputrasya navamasya manorghṛtiketvādiputrāṇāṃ medhātithyādisaptaṣīṇāṃ parādidevagaṇānāṃ vibhunāmno bhaviṣyadindrasya kālakakṣādidevadāyādarājño vasunābhasya dhārmikatvādbhaviṣyadviṣṇuputratayā bhāvikālakālakākṣavadhaḥ
1.191.d: 184 ब्रह्मपुत्रस्य नवमस्य मनोर्घृतिकेत्वादिपुत्राणां मेधातिथ्यादिसप्तषीणां परादिदेवगणानां विभुनाम्नो भविष्यदिन्द्रस्य कालकक्षादिदेवदायादराज्ञो वसुनाभस्य धार्मिकत्वाद्भविष्यद्विष्णुपुत्रतया भाविकालकालकाक्षवधः
1.191.m: 184 Of the ninth Manu, the son of Brahmā, the sons beginning with Dhṛtiketu, the seven seers beginning with Medhātithi, the groups of gods beginning with the Paras, the future Indra named Vibhu; because of the righteousness of King Vasunābha, an heir of the gods [opposed by] Kālakākṣa and others, he will be a future son of Viṣṇu, [leading to] the future slaying of Kālaka and Kālākṣa.

1.191.s:
185 dharmaputrasya daśamasya manoḥ sukṣetrādiputrāṇāmāpomūrtyādisaptarṣīṇāṃ prāṇākhyādidevagaṇānāmindrasya śāntyākhyasya tadvidviṣā prabalasya
vālino viṣṇukartṛkaṃ hananam
1.191.d:
185 धर्मपुत्रस्य दशमस्य मनोः सुक्षेत्रादिपुत्राणामापोमूर्त्यादिसप्तर्षीणां प्राणाख्यादिदेवगणानामिन्द्रस्य शान्त्याख्यस्य तद्विद्विषा प्रबलस्य
वालिनो विष्णुकर्तृकं हननम्
1.191.m: 185. An account of the sons of the tenth Manu, the son of Dharma, such as Sukṣetra; the seven sages, such as Āpomūrti; the classes of gods, such as the Prāṇas; the Indra named Śānti; and the killing of his mighty enemy Vālin by Viṣṇu.

1.191.s: 186 rudraputrasryakādaśasya manoḥ sarvartugādiputrāṇāṃ haviṣmadādisaptarṣīṇāṃ nirmathyādidevagaṇānāmindrasya vṛṣābhidheyasya dviṣantaṃ daśagrīvaṃ viṣṇuḥ straiṇaṃ rūpamāśrito vadhiṣyati ..
1.191.d: 186 रुद्रपुत्रस्र्यकादशस्य मनोः सर्वर्तुगादिपुत्राणां हविष्मदादिसप्तर्षीणां निर्मथ्यादिदेवगणानामिन्द्रस्य वृषाभिधेयस्य द्विषन्तं दशग्रीवं विष्णुः स्त्रैणं रूपमाश्रितो वधिष्यति ॥
1.191.m: 186. An account of the sons of the eleventh Manu, the son of Rudra, such as Sarvartuga; the seven sages, such as Haviṣmat; the classes of gods, such as the Nirmathyas; the Indra named Vṛṣa; and how Viṣṇu, having assumed a female form, will slay his enemy Daśagrīva.

1.191.s: 187 dvādaśasya manordakṣaputrasya devavadādiputrāṇāṃ sattamādisaptarṣīṇāṃ suśarmādidevagaṇānāmindrasyārātiṃ naraka napuṃsakarūpeṇa viṣṇurhantā
1.191.d: 187 द्वादशस्य मनोर्दक्षपुत्रस्य देववदादिपुत्राणां सत्तमादिसप्तर्षीणां सुशर्मादिदेवगणानामिन्द्रस्यारातिं नरक नपुंसकरूपेण विष्णुर्हन्ता
1.191.m: 187. An account of the sons of the twelfth Manu, the son of Dakṣa, such as Devavat; the seven sages, such as Sattama; the classes of gods, such as Suśarman; and how Viṣṇu, in the form of a eunuch, will slay Naraka, the enemy of Indra.

1.191.s: 188 trayodaśasya raucyasya manościtrasenādiputrāṇāṃ dhṛtimadādisaptarṣīṇāṃ sutrāmādidevagaṇānāmindrasya bṛhaspaterasuradāyādasya ṭiṭṭibhasya māyūrarūpiviṣṇunā vināśaḥ
1.191.d: 188 त्रयोदशस्य रौच्यस्य मनोश्चित्रसेनादिपुत्राणां धृतिमदादिसप्तर्षीणां सुत्रामादिदेवगणानामिन्द्रस्य बृहस्पतेरसुरदायादस्य टिट्टिभस्य मायूररूपिविष्णुना विनाशः
1.191.m: 188. An account of the sons of the thirteenth Manu, Raupya, such as Citrasena; the seven sages, such as Dhṛtimat; the classes of gods, such as Sutrāman; the Indra Bṛhaspati; and the destruction of the Asura heir Ṭiṭṭibha by Viṣṇu in the form of a peacock.

1.191.s: 189 caturdaśasya bhautyasya manostaraṃgabhedābhidādiputrāṇāmagnīdhrādisaptarṣīṇāṃ cākṣuṣādidevagaṇānāṃ śucerindrasya śatrūṇāṃ rājño mahāsukhasya samaye divyavarṣasahasraparyantaṃ devāsurayuddhe jāte tāmasīmāyayā madhusūdano rīnvadhiṣyati .|
1.191.d: 189 चतुर्दशस्य भौत्यस्य मनोस्तरंगभेदाभिदादिपुत्राणामग्नीध्रादिसप्तर्षीणां चाक्षुषादिदेवगणानां शुचेरिन्द्रस्य शत्रूणां राज्ञो महासुखस्य समये दिव्यवर्षसहस्रपर्यन्तं देवासुरयुद्धे जाते तामसीमायया मधुसूदनो रीन्वधिष्यति ॥
1.191.m: 189. An account of the sons of the fourteenth Manu, Bhautya, such as Taraṅgabheda and Abhidā; the seven sages, such as Agnīdhra; the classes of gods, such as the Cākṣuṣas; the Indra Śuci; and how, when a war between the gods and Asuras occurs for a thousand divine years during the time of King Mahāsukha, Madhusūdana will slay the enemies of Indra by means of tāmasika delusion.
190. Viṣṇu's assumption of many incarnations in each age according to the task at hand.

1.191.s: 191 śakrapraśnānurodhena śāmbarāyaṇyā yāvajjīvaṃ māsanakṣatrapūjanena svasyā atītānāgatamanvantareṣu tadvṛttajñānam
1.191.d: 191 शक्रप्रश्नानुरोधेन शाम्बरायण्या यावज्जीवं मासनक्षत्रपूजनेन स्वस्या अतीतानागतमन्वन्तरेषु तद्वृत्तज्ञानम्
1.191.m: 191. Śāmbarāyaṇī's knowledge of the events in past and future manvantaras through lifelong worship of the months and lunar mansions, in response to Śakra's question.
192. Description of the hymn of praise and the greatness of Śrī Viṣṇu.
193. The transformation of Hāhā and Hūhū into an elephant and a crocodile through disrespect toward the sage Devala.

1.191.s:
194 jambūdvīpe śrṛṅgavati kulācale hāhāgandharvasya hastitvena huhvo nakratvena ca nivasatormadhyāhne jalaṃ pātumantaḥsarasi praviṣṭe gajarāje raudreṇa
grāheṇa tasya grahaṇaṃ mitho yuddhe gajarājena puṣkarāgradhūtakamalapuṣpeṇa viṣṇormānasikasaparyā vyadhāyi tadbhāvākṛṣṭo viṣṇuḥ sarasi tatsānnidhyaṃ kalpayitvobhāvapi gandharvatāmanayata etadadhyāyapaṭhanaphalam
1.191.d:
194 जम्बूद्वीपे श्रृङ्गवति कुलाचले हाहागन्धर्वस्य हस्तित्वेन हुह्वो नक्रत्वेन च निवसतोर्मध्याह्ने जलं पातुमन्तःसरसि प्रविष्टे गजराजे रौद्रेण
ग्राहेण तस्य ग्रहणं मिथो युद्धे गजराजेन पुष्कराग्रधूतकमलपुष्पेण विष्णोर्मानसिकसपर्या व्यधायि तद्भावाकृष्टो विष्णुः सरसि तत्सान्निध्यं कल्पयित्वोभावपि गन्धर्वतामनयत एतदध्यायपठनफलम्
1.191.m: 194. On the Śṛṅgavat mountain range in Jambūdvīpa, the Gandharva Hāhā living as an elephant and Hūhū living as a crocodile: when the lordly elephant entered the lake at midday to drink water, his capture by the fierce water-monster; in their mutual combat, the mental worship of Viṣṇu performed by the lordly elephant with a lotus flower shaken by the tip of his trunk; drawn by that devotion, Viṣṇu, having manifested his presence at the lake, brought them both back to the state of Gandharvas; and the fruit of reciting this chapter.
195. The Viṣṇupañjara hymn, which pacifies all wicked beings.

1.191.s: 196 brahmaṇā tripuraṃ jighāṃsoḥ śaṅkarasya rakṣāyai, , vāgīśena ca balaṃ jighāṃsoḥ śakrasya rakṣāyai nirūpitasya viṣṇupañjarastotrasya kathanam...
1.191.d: 196 ब्रह्मणा त्रिपुरं जिघांसोः शङ्करस्य रक्षायै, , वागीशेन च बलं जिघांसोः शक्रस्य रक्षायै निरूपितस्य विष्णुपञ्जरस्तोत्रस्य कथनम्॥।
1.191.m: 196. The recitation of the Viṣṇupañjara hymn, prescribed by Brahmā for the protection of Śaṅkara when he wished to destroy Tripura, and by the Lord of Speech for the protection of Śakra when he wished to destroy Bala.
197. The origin of the Yakṣas from Kaśyapa through his wife named Khaśā.

1.191.s: 198 kapiṣāsutayorajaṣaṇḍhayorbrahmadhānayātudhānākhye tanaye babhūvatuḥ, tau te kanyake kṣudhitākāraṃ rākṣasaṃ dadatuḥ, tasya brahmadhānānvaye brahmadhānā niśācarāḥ, yātudhānānvaye yātudhānāḥ prasiddhāḥ . śleṣmātakavanasthāneṣu daśabrahmarākṣaseṣu sūryānucareṣu hetiprahetivaṃśyeṣu mālisumāli mālyavatsu sumālidauhitrastrilokavijayī rāvaṇaḥ, mālino dhareṇa vasunā nidhanaṃ mālyavāṃśca varṣatmā sukhaṃ jīvati
1.191.d: 198 कपिषासुतयोरजषण्ढयोर्ब्रह्मधानयातुधानाख्ये तनये बभूवतुः, तौ ते कन्यके क्षुधिताकारं राक्षसं ददतुः, तस्य ब्रह्मधानान्वये ब्रह्मधाना निशाचराः, यातुधानान्वये यातुधानाः प्रसिद्धाः । श्लेष्मातकवनस्थानेषु दशब्रह्मराक्षसेषु सूर्यानुचरेषु हेतिप्रहेतिवंश्येषु मालिसुमालि माल्यवत्सु सुमालिदौहित्रस्त्रिलोकविजयी रावणः, मालिनो धरेण वसुना निधनं माल्यवांश्च वर्षत्मा सुखं जीवति
1.191.m: 198. The two daughters of Kapiṣā, Aja and Ṣaṇḍhā, bore two sons named Brahmadhāna and Yātudhāna; they gave those two maidens to a hungry-looking Rākṣasa; in his Brahmadhāna lineage, the Brahmadhāna night-wanderers became famous, and in his Yātudhāna lineage, the Yātudhānas; among the ten Brahmarākṣasas dwelling in the Śleṣmātaka forest, companions of the sun, descendants of Heti and Praheti, namely Māli, Sumāli, and Mālyavat, Rāvaṇa, the conqueror of the three worlds, was the maternal grandson of Sumāli; Māli met his death at the hands of the Vasu Dhara, while Mālyavat, possessing an aged body, lives happily.

1.191.s: 199 pulomadānavendreṇa svajyeṣṭhatanayā pulomajā bhṛgave dattā, ekadā'ntarvatnīmagnihotragatāṃ tāṃ pulomā rākṣaso'bhyetya he'gne matpūrveyaṃ navetyuktavān, neyaṃ tvatpūrveti śrutvā'pi sa tāṃ jahāra, pathi garbhacyuteścyavana iti garbhajātasya saṃjñā, tena dṛṣṭamātrasya rakṣaso nāśaḥ pulomāśrunipātena vadhūvarānadīprārdubhāvo bhṛgoḥ sakāśādagneḥ sarvabhakṣakatvaśāpaḥ, brahmaṇāgneranugrahaśca .
1.191.d: 199 पुलोमदानवेन्द्रेण स्वज्येष्ठतनया पुलोमजा भृगवे दत्ता, एकदाऽन्तर्वत्नीमग्निहोत्रगतां तां पुलोमा राक्षसोऽभ्येत्य हेऽग्ने मत्पूर्वेयं नवेत्युक्तवान्, नेयं त्वत्पूर्वेति श्रुत्वाऽपि स तां जहार, पथि गर्भच्युतेश्च्यवन इति गर्भजातस्य संज्ञा, तेन दृष्टमात्रस्य रक्षसो नाशः पुलोमाश्रुनिपातेन वधूवरानदीप्रार्दुभावो भृगोः सकाशादग्नेः सर्वभक्षकत्वशापः, ब्रह्मणाग्नेरनुग्रहश्च ।
1.191.m: 199. Pulomajā, the eldest daughter of Puloman, the lord of the Dānavas, was given to Bhṛgu; once, when she was pregnant and had gone to the fire-sanctuary, the Rākṣasa Puloman approached and said, 'O Fire, was she not mine first?'; even after hearing 'She was not yours first,' he abducted her; because of the fall of the fetus on the path, the one born from the womb was named Cyavana; by his mere glance, the Rākṣasa was destroyed; from the falling of Pulomā's tears, the river Vadhūsaras appeared; the curse of consuming everything [laid] upon Fire by Bhṛgu, and the grace bestowed upon Fire by Brahmā.

1.191.s: 200 svatapasā haraṃ prasādya labdhaśūlo madhudaityo rāvaṇasvāsāraṃ kumbhīlasīṃ hṛtvā tasyāṃ lavaṇaṃ sutamutpādayāmāsa, māndhātārañca yuddhe jaghāna
1.191.d: 200 स्वतपसा हरं प्रसाद्य लब्धशूलो मधुदैत्यो रावणस्वासारं कुम्भीलसीं हृत्वा तस्यां लवणं सुतमुत्पादयामास, मान्धातारञ्च युद्धे जघान
1.191.m: 200. The Daitya Madhu, having pleased Hara through his own austerities and obtained a trident, abducted Rāvaṇa's sister Kumbhīnasī, begot on her a son named Lavaṇa, and killed Māndhātṛ in battle.
201. Description of the lineage of Śailūṣa.
202. Description of Bharata's departure to conquer the wicked Śailūṣa Gandharvas.

1.191.s: 203 bharatayuddhayātrāyāṃ trilakṣasaṃkhyākānāmaśvānāṃ daśasahasrāṇāṃ dantināṃ ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇāṃ rathānāṃ pañcakoṭipadātṝnāṃ vastrasuvarṇamaṇyādīnāṃ nicayaiḥ saha bahupaṇyayuktavaṇigādiviṣavaidyakāmavaidyakarmantikasthapatimārgikādīnāṃ preṣaṇam
1.191.d: 203 भरतयुद्धयात्रायां त्रिलक्षसंख्याकानामश्वानां दशसहस्राणां दन्तिनां षष्टिसहस्राणां रथानां पञ्चकोटिपदातॄनां वस्त्रसुवर्णमण्यादीनां निचयैः सह बहुपण्ययुक्तवणिगादिविषवैद्यकामवैद्यकर्मन्तिकस्थपतिमार्गिकादीनां प्रेषणम्
1.191.m: 203. On Bharata's military expedition, the dispatching of three hundred thousand horses, ten thousand elephants, sixty thousand chariots, and fifty million foot-soldiers, along with heaps of garments, gold, jewels, and other treasures, as well as merchants provided with abundant merchandise, physicians for poison, specialists in aphrodisiacs, superintendents of works, architects, road-builders, and others.

1.191.s: 204 bharatamāśīrvādairabhivarddhya gandharvānhatvā. sindhorubhayapārśvayornagare nirmāpyobhau putrau tatrābhiṣicya yudhājitaṃ sammānya ca śīghamāgacchetyādi śrīrāmeṇa samantraṇam, sa krośamātre sthāne nirmitaṃ śiviraṃ praviśya paurajānapadaṃ ca visarjyotaradainikakarmasūcanārthaṃ ḍiṇḍimadhvanikaraṇādikaṃ lakṣmaṇamupadideśa
1.191.d: 204 भरतमाशीर्वादैरभिवर्द्ध्य गन्धर्वान्हत्वा। सिन्धोरुभयपार्श्वयोर्नगरे निर्माप्योभौ पुत्रौ तत्राभिषिच्य युधाजितं सम्मान्य च शीघमागच्छेत्यादि श्रीरामेण समन्त्रणम्, स क्रोशमात्रे स्थाने निर्मितं शिविरं प्रविश्य पौरजानपदं च विसर्ज्योतरदैनिककर्मसूचनार्थं डिण्डिमध्वनिकरणादिकं लक्ष्मणमुपदिदेश
1.191.m: 204. Having encouraged Bharata with blessings, [saying,] 'Kill the Gandharvas, build two cities on both banks of the Indus, consecrate both your sons there, honor Yudhājit, and return quickly,' and other counsel from Śrī Rāma; Bharata entered the camp constructed at a distance of merely a krośa, dismissed the citizens and countryfolk, and instructed Lakṣmaṇa regarding the sounding of drums and the like to signal the next day's duties.

1.191.s: 205 prāyāṇikavādyaghoṣabṛṃhitaheṣitāditumule prayāntīnāṃ bharatāvarodharāmāṇāṃ dīnāndhakṛpaṇādibhyo dānadayādivarṇanapurassaraṃ prāyāṇikakṛtyanirdeśaḥ
1.191.d: 205 प्रायाणिकवाद्यघोषबृंहितहेषितादितुमुले प्रयान्तीनां भरतावरोधरामाणां दीनान्धकृपणादिभ्यो दानदयादिवर्णनपुरस्सरं प्रायाणिककृत्यनिर्देशः
1.191.m: 205. In the tumult of the marching musical instruments, trumpeting, neighing, and the like, as the women of Bharata's inner apartments set forth, the direction of duties on the march, preceded by a description of charity, compassion, and so forth toward the poor, the blind, and the destitute.

1.191.s: 206 gaṃgāyāṃ snānaśrāddhadānādidhārmikakriyānantaramaparapāragamanāya kūṭāgāradīpavṛkṣādinirmāṇāya ca bharatasya nideśānantaraṃ niśāyāmeva naukādibhistaraṇam
1.191.d: 206 गंगायां स्नानश्राद्धदानादिधार्मिकक्रियानन्तरमपरपारगमनाय कूटागारदीपवृक्षादिनिर्माणाय च भरतस्य निदेशानन्तरं निशायामेव नौकादिभिस्तरणम्
1.191.m: 206. After performing pious rites such as bathing, ancestral offerings, and gifts at the Gaṅgā, and after Bharata's command to construct temporary pavilions, lamp-trees, and the like in order to cross to the other shore, the crossing by boats and the like even in the night.

1.191.s: 207 mārge bharatasya damanakirātena saṃgamaḥ, yamunāyāṃ snānadānaśrāddhāderanantaraṃ matsyasālvādinṛpaiḥ saṃgatya bharatena kurukṣetrasya tīrthasannītināmadheyakāraṇe pṛṣṭe ghaṭodarabrāhmaṇena cyāvanadadhīcyasthinirmitavajreṇa daityanāśasya tathā māsaparyaṃtaṃ sarvatīrthānāṃ kurukṣetre sannidhānasya kāraṇamavoci, tato'marakaṇṭakāditīrtheṣu snānādikaṃ kṛtvā devikānadyāṃ bharate gate kumārādipañcaparvatīyarājñāṃ tadabhyāśe āgamanaṃ tatra trirātramuṣitvā bharataścandrabhāgāṃ yayau. punaśca vitastāmuttīrya kaikayānāpya sa yudhājitā tanmātulena satkṛtaḥ
1.191.d: 207 मार्गे भरतस्य दमनकिरातेन संगमः, यमुनायां स्नानदानश्राद्धादेरनन्तरं मत्स्यसाल्वादिनृपैः संगत्य भरतेन कुरुक्षेत्रस्य तीर्थसन्नीतिनामधेयकारणे पृष्टे घटोदरब्राह्मणेन च्यावनदधीच्यस्थिनिर्मितवज्रेण दैत्यनाशस्य तथा मासपर्यंतं सर्वतीर्थानां कुरुक्षेत्रे सन्निधानस्य कारणमवोचि, ततोऽमरकण्टकादितीर्थेषु स्नानादिकं कृत्वा देविकानद्यां भरते गते कुमारादिपञ्चपर्वतीयराज्ञां तदभ्याशे आगमनं तत्र त्रिरात्रमुषित्वा भरतश्चन्द्रभागां ययौ। पुनश्च वितस्तामुत्तीर्य कैकयानाप्य स युधाजिता तन्मातुलेन सत्कृतः
1.191.m: 207. On the road, Bharata's encounter with the Damanakirāta; after bathing, giving gifts, ancestral offerings, and the like at the Yamunā, meeting with kings such as the Matsyas and Sālvas; when Bharata inquired about the reason for the name of the sacred bathing-place Kurukṣetra as Sannīti, the reason was explained by the brahmin Ghaṭodara as the destruction of the Daityas by the thunderbolt made from the bones of Dadhīca, the descendant of Cyavana, and the presence of all sacred bathing-places at Kurukṣetra for the period of a month; then, having bathed and performed other rites at sacred bathing-places such as Amarakaṇṭaka, when Bharata went to the Devikā river, the arrival into his presence of five mountain kings headed by Kumāra; after residing there for three nights, Bharata went to the Candrabhāgā; and further, having crossed the Vitastā and reached the Kekayas, he was honored by Yudhājit, his maternal uncle.

1.191.s: 208 pradyumnāṃśasamutpannetidarśanīye bharate yudhājitpuraṃ praviṣṭe paurastriyo vismṛtasakalavyāpārā niśceṣṭāstaṃ dadṛśuḥ, bharataśca mātulagṛhaṃ prāpya parārdhyabhojanapānādisatkāraṃ lebhe
1.191.d: 208 प्रद्युम्नांशसमुत्पन्नेतिदर्शनीये भरते युधाजित्पुरं प्रविष्टे पौरस्त्रियो विस्मृतसकलव्यापारा निश्चेष्टास्तं ददृशुः, भरतश्च मातुलगृहं प्राप्य परार्ध्यभोजनपानादिसत्कारं लेभे
1.191.m: 208. When Bharata, born from a portion of Pradyumna and exceedingly handsome to behold, entered the city of Yudhājit, the women of the city, forgetting all their tasks, watched him motionless; and Bharata, having reached his maternal uncle's house, received hospitality consisting of the finest food, drink, and the like.

1.191.s:
209 bharato bandināṃ vicitrā navyā bhavyāśca racanāḥ śṛṇvannutthāya kṛtasandhyāhavanatarpaṇādinityakriyo brāhmaṇāndhanadānena tutoṣa, punaśva sabhāṃ gato tapodhanairdvijavaraiḥ kṛtāśīrvādo balamukhyānmahīpatīṃśca dadarśa, svadattatāmbūlena sapraśrayaṃ tānvisasarja ca tato yuddhāya maṃtraṇe jāte gārgyaṃ dautyakarmaṇi niyujya śve yoddhavyamiti ājñāpayāmāsa, sandhyāmupāsya gūḍhabhāṣitamākarṇya ca prāsādātsainikānāṃ pavanānaya
nākṣveḍāśabdādivṛtāntadarśanaśravaṇābhyāṃ mudamāpa
1.191.d:
209 भरतो बन्दिनां विचित्रा नव्या भव्याश्च रचनाः शृण्वन्नुत्थाय कृतसन्ध्याहवनतर्पणादिनित्यक्रियो ब्राह्मणान्धनदानेन तुतोष, पुनश्व सभां गतो तपोधनैर्द्विजवरैः कृताशीर्वादो बलमुख्यान्महीपतींश्च ददर्श, स्वदत्तताम्बूलेन सप्रश्रयं तान्विससर्ज च ततो युद्धाय मंत्रणे जाते गार्ग्यं दौत्यकर्मणि नियुज्य श्वे योद्धव्यमिति आज्ञापयामास, सन्ध्यामुपास्य गूढभाषितमाकर्ण्य च प्रासादात्सैनिकानां पवनानय
नाक्ष्वेडाशब्दादिवृतान्तदर्शनश्रवणाभ्यां मुदमाप
1.191.m: 209 Bharata, rising while listening to the diverse, novel, and splendid compositions of the bards, performed his daily rites such as the twilight worship, fire-offering, and water-libations, and satisfied the brahmins with gifts of wealth; having gone again to the assembly, he was blessed by the foremost of the twice-born rich in asceticism, and received the chiefs of the army and the kings, and dismissed them with modesty after offering betel with his own hand; then, after consultations were held for battle, he appointed Gārgya to the task of an envoy and ordered, "Tomorrow battle is to be joined"; having performed the evening twilight worship and heard secret counsel, he derived joy from the palace by seeing and hearing the tidings of the soldiers, including the catching of the wind, the twanging of bows, and the roaring sounds.

1.191.s: 210 bharatāhvānadundubhi śrutvā śalūṣatanayāḥ śailūṣaṃ rājānamupatasthuḥ bharatasaṃdiṣṭaṃ gārgyavākyaṃ saroṣaṃ mantrayāmāsuśca
1.191.d: 210 भरताह्वानदुन्दुभि श्रुत्वा शलूषतनयाः शैलूषं राजानमुपतस्थुः भरतसंदिष्टं गार्ग्यवाक्यं सरोषं मन्त्रयामासुश्च
1.191.m: 210 Having heard the kettledrum sounding Bharata's challenge, the sons of Śailūṣa approached King Śailūṣa and, filled with anger, deliberated upon Gārgya's message sent by Bharata.
211 The granting of consent regarding battle by the assembly members, such as Aparājita, addressed to the king of the gandharvas.

1.191.s: 212 kṛṣivāṇijyādikarmopayoginī bhūrmānuṣāṇāmevopayujyate kintayā devajātīyānāṃ gandharvāṇām, bharataśca pradyumnāṃśaḥ sumālinamapyavadhīttena sārdhaṃ vigraho na vidvatsammata iti nāḍāyano'mantrayata
1.191.d: 212 कृषिवाणिज्यादिकर्मोपयोगिनी भूर्मानुषाणामेवोपयुज्यते किन्तया देवजातीयानां गन्धर्वाणाम्, भरतश्च प्रद्युम्नांशः सुमालिनमप्यवधीत्तेन सार्धं विग्रहो न विद्वत्सम्मत इति नाडायनोऽमन्त्रयत
1.191.m: 212 "Land suitable for works such as agriculture and commerce is useful only for human beings; what need of it have the gandharvas, who belong to the divine race? Moreover, Bharata is a portion of Pradyumna and he even slew Sumālin; war with him is not approved by the wise," thus Nāḍāyana advised.

1.191.s: 213 vṛtre śakreṇa nihate daityāḥ samudramabdurgaṃ vidhāya rātrau prajā nijaghnuḥ, suraprārthito'gastyaḥ samudraṃ papau tena duṣṭadaityanāśaḥ samajani . raviniśākaramārgaṃ roddhuṃ pravṛtte vindhyagirāvagastyena svapraṇāmakaraṇāya namre tasminmama pratyāgamanaparyantamevameva nīcaistiṣṭhetyadyāpi tasya kharvatākaraṇam, ilvalavātāpinorbhakṣaṇena śaradi tvayyudite'pāmamalatvaṃ tava ca loke pūjā bhaviṣyatītyādyagastyāya devairvaradānam
1.191.d: 213 वृत्रे शक्रेण निहते दैत्याः समुद्रमब्दुर्गं विधाय रात्रौ प्रजा निजघ्नुः, सुरप्रार्थितोऽगस्त्यः समुद्रं पपौ तेन दुष्टदैत्यनाशः समजनि । रविनिशाकरमार्गं रोद्धुं प्रवृत्ते विन्ध्यगिरावगस्त्येन स्वप्रणामकरणाय नम्रे तस्मिन्मम प्रत्यागमनपर्यन्तमेवमेव नीचैस्तिष्ठेत्यद्यापि तस्य खर्वताकरणम्, इल्वलवातापिनोर्भक्षणेन शरदि त्वय्युदितेऽपाममलत्वं तव च लोके पूजा भविष्यतीत्याद्यगस्त्याय देवैर्वरदानम्
1.191.m: 213 When Vṛtra was slain by Śakra, the daityas made the ocean an inaccessible fortress and slaughtered the creatures at night; Agastya, petitioned by the gods, drank up the ocean, whereby the destruction of the wicked daityas came about. When the Vindhya mountain set about blocking the path of the sun and moon, he bowed down to pay his respects to Agastya, who told him, "Remain low just like this until my return," which is the cause of its dwarf stature even today. Through his consumption of Ilvala and Vātāpi, the gods granted boons to Agastya, saying, "Upon your rising in the autumn, waters will become pure and there will be worship of you in the world," and so forth.

1.191.s: 214 mālyavatā vāryyamāṇāvapi mālisumālinau laṃkādurgamāśritya devānpīḍayāñcakratuḥ tataśca brahmeśasahitā devāḥ kṣīrapayodhau suptaṃ viṣṇumupatasthire
1.191.d: 214 माल्यवता वार्य्यमाणावपि मालिसुमालिनौ लंकादुर्गमाश्रित्य देवान्पीडयाञ्चक्रतुः ततश्च ब्रह्मेशसहिता देवाः क्षीरपयोधौ सुप्तं विष्णुमुपतस्थिरे
1.191.m: 214 Though restrained by Mālyavat, Māli and Sumālin resorted to the fortress of Laṅkā and tormented the gods; thereupon the gods, accompanied by Brahmā and Śiva, approached Viṣṇu sleeping upon the milk-ocean.
215 All the gods, sages, rivers, and streams followed Śrī Viṣṇu […].
216 Having heard of the gods' preparation for battle, Māli and Sumālin set out for war.
217 In the battle between the gods and asuras, Viṣṇu severed the head of the rākṣasa Māli […].

1.191.s: 218 mālinidhanānantaraṃ tārkṣyapakṣavātatāḍitarakṣasāṃ pātālagamanaṃ laṅkāyā vaiśravaṇe dānam
1.191.d: 218 मालिनिधनानन्तरं तार्क्ष्यपक्षवातताडितरक्षसां पातालगमनं लङ्काया वैश्रवणे दानम्
1.191.m: 218 After the death of Māli, the rākṣasas, struck by the wind of Tārkṣya's wings, went to Pātāla, and Laṅkā was given to Vaiśravaṇa.

1.191.s: 219 brahmamānasaputrapulastyasya viśravaso bṛhaspatipautrī bharadvājasutā devavarṇinī bhāryā''sīt tatputrāya vaiśravaṇāya tattapastuṣṭo brahmā yakṣeśadhaneśalokapālatvaṃ vitīrya puṣpakaṃ vimānaṃ viśvakarmanirmitāṃ laṃkāṃ ca dadau ..
1.191.d: 219 ब्रह्ममानसपुत्रपुलस्त्यस्य विश्रवसो बृहस्पतिपौत्री भरद्वाजसुता देववर्णिनी भार्या'ऽसीत् तत्पुत्राय वैश्रवणाय तत्तपस्तुष्टो ब्रह्मा यक्षेशधनेशलोकपालत्वं वितीर्य पुष्पकं विमानं विश्वकर्मनिर्मितां लंकां च ददौ ॥
1.191.m: 219 The wife of Viśravas, son of Pulastya who was the mind-born son of Brahmā, was Devavarṇinī, the daughter of Bharadvāja and granddaughter of Bṛhaspati; Brahmā, pleased by his austerities, bestowed upon her son Vaiśravaṇa the status of lord of the yakṣas, lord of wealth, and guardian of the worlds, and gave him the Puṣpaka aerial car and Laṅkā fashioned by Viśvakarman.

1.191.s: 220 sumālinaḥ piturādeśātkaikasyā viśravasaḥ rāvaṇakumbhakarṇayoḥ sutayoḥ śūrpaṇakhāyāḥ kanyāyāścotpattiḥ, kadāciddhanādhyakṣavaibhavaṃ darśayantī kaikasī rāvaṇamūce tvamapyevaṃ śrīmānbhaveti, tataśca brahmaṇaḥ sakāśānmānuṣaṃ vihāya devādibhyo'vadhaṃ trailokyaviṣayañca yayāce, evaṃ vibhīṣaṇaṃ nityaṃ dharmamatimamaratvañca dattvā brahmaṇi yāte pātālādrakṣāṃsyāgatya daśavaktraṃ laṃkārājye'bhyaṣecayan . rāvaṇavacanātkubero laṃkāṃ tyaktvā'lakāyāmavasat punaśca trailokyavijayaṃ kṛtvā mayatanayāṃ mandodarīṃ rāvaṇa upayeme, tasyāśca meghanādaṃ sūnuṃ janayāmāsa sa rāmeṇāvadhi
1.191.d: 220 सुमालिनः पितुरादेशात्कैकस्या विश्रवसः रावणकुम्भकर्णयोः सुतयोः शूर्पणखायाः कन्यायाश्चोत्पत्तिः, कदाचिद्धनाध्यक्षवैभवं दर्शयन्ती कैकसी रावणमूचे त्वमप्येवं श्रीमान्भवेति, ततश्च ब्रह्मणः सकाशान्मानुषं विहाय देवादिभ्योऽवधं त्रैलोक्यविषयञ्च ययाचे, एवं विभीषणं नित्यं धर्ममतिममरत्वञ्च दत्त्वा ब्रह्मणि याते पातालाद्रक्षांस्यागत्य दशवक्त्रं लंकाराज्येऽभ्यषेचयन् । रावणवचनात्कुबेरो लंकां त्यक्त्वाऽलकायामवसत् पुनश्च त्रैलोक्यविजयं कृत्वा मयतनयां मन्दोदरीं रावण उपयेमे, तस्याश्च मेघनादं सूनुं जनयामास स रामेणावधि
1.191.m: 220 By the instruction of her father Sumālin, the birth of two sons, Rāvaṇa and Kumbhakarṇa, and a daughter, Śūrpaṇakhā, took place from Kaikasī by Viśravas; once, showing the majesty of the lord of wealth, Kaikasī said to Rāvaṇa, "You too become glorious like this"; thereupon, he requested from Brahmā invulnerability from gods and others, excluding human beings, and lordship over the three worlds; when Brahmā departed after thus bestowing upon Vibhīṣaṇa constant devotion to dharma and immortality, the rākṣasas came from Pātāla and consecrated the ten-faced one to the kingdom of Laṅkā. At Rāvaṇa's word, Kubera left Laṅkā and dwelt in Alakā; then, having conquered the three worlds, Rāvaṇa married Mandodarī, the daughter of Maya, and fathered upon her a son, Meghanāda, who was [later] slain by Rāma.

1.191.s: 221 brahmadattavaradṛpto rāvaṇastridaśarāmāḥ kanyāśca jahāra, ayodhyāvāsyanaraṇyaṃ nṛpaṃ jaghāna sa ca matkulyāttava nidhanaṃ bhaviṣyatīti tamaśapat . maruttayajñe devāparādhaṃ ca kṛtavān, bṛhaspatisutakuśadhvajakanyā vedavatīti khyātā viṣṇupatyarthaṃ tapasyantī rāvaṇena pralobhitāpi na taṃ cakame, keśapāśe tena spṛṣṭā sā jvalanaṃ praviṣṭā'nyajanmani sītā babhūva, saṃkṣipya rāmasītācaritamuktvā tādṛśaviṣṇubhrātṛbharatena yuddhaṃ na śreya iti nāḍāyanasammatiḥ .
1.191.d: 221 ब्रह्मदत्तवरदृप्तो रावणस्त्रिदशरामाः कन्याश्च जहार, अयोध्यावास्यनरण्यं नृपं जघान स च मत्कुल्यात्तव निधनं भविष्यतीति तमशपत् । मरुत्तयज्ञे देवापराधं च कृतवान्, बृहस्पतिसुतकुशध्वजकन्या वेदवतीति ख्याता विष्णुपत्यर्थं तपस्यन्ती रावणेन प्रलोभितापि न तं चकमे, केशपाशे तेन स्पृष्टा सा ज्वलनं प्रविष्टाऽन्यजन्मनि सीता बभूव, संक्षिप्य रामसीताचरितमुक्त्वा तादृशविष्णुभ्रातृभरतेन युद्धं न श्रेय इति नाडायनसम्मतिः ।
1.191.m: 221 Proud with the boons granted by Brahmā, Rāvaṇa abducted the women and maidens of the thirty [gods]; he slew the king Anaraṇya, a dweller of Ayodhyā, who cursed him, saying, "Your destruction will come from one of my lineage"; and he committed an offense against the gods at the sacrifice of Marutta; the daughter of Kuśadhvaja, the son of Bṛhaspati, celebrated as Vedavatī, practicing austerities to obtain Viṣṇu as her husband, did not desire Rāvaṇa though enticed by him; touched by him on her mass of hair, she entered the fire and in another birth became Sītā. Having related the deeds of Rāma and Sītā in brief, Nāḍāyana's opinion is: "War with Bharata, who is the brother of such a Viṣṇu, is not beneficial."

1.191.s: 222 mauddhatyaṃ kṛthāḥ suraistvadvadhaścintyata iti vaktāraṃ dhanadadūtaṃ hatvā tasya puṣpakavimānaṃ ca hṛtvā rāvaṇaḥ kailāśaṃ yayau, vānarākṛtiṃ nandinaṃ dṛṣṭvā prahasati rāvaṇe pulahaprajāpatikulasambhūtavānarebhyastava vināśaḥ syāditi nandikeśvaraśāpe jāte sakailāsaṃ haraṃ laṅkāṃ ninīṣau rāvaṇe, acalacalanasambhramajātasvayaṃgrahomā''śleṣatuṣṭo harastaṃ rāvaṇanāmānamakarot, tataśca rāvaṇaḥ saṃyaminyāṃ dharmarājaṃ kālapāśayāgapitṛgaṇāṃśca vijitya sūryeṇa yoddhumupatasthau, brahmā sūryaṃ nyavārayadrāvaṇaśca sendrāndevānvijigye .
1.191.d: 222 मौद्धत्यं कृथाः सुरैस्त्वद्वधश्चिन्त्यत इति वक्तारं धनददूतं हत्वा तस्य पुष्पकविमानं च हृत्वा रावणः कैलाशं ययौ, वानराकृतिं नन्दिनं दृष्ट्वा प्रहसति रावणे पुलहप्रजापतिकुलसम्भूतवानरेभ्यस्तव विनाशः स्यादिति नन्दिकेश्वरशापे जाते सकैलासं हरं लङ्कां निनीषौ रावणे, अचलचलनसम्भ्रमजातस्वयंग्रहोमा'ऽश्लेषतुष्टो हरस्तं रावणनामानमकरोत्, ततश्च रावणः संयमिन्यां धर्मराजं कालपाशयागपितृगणांश्च विजित्य सूर्येण योद्धुमुपतस्थौ, ब्रह्मा सूर्यं न्यवारयद्रावणश्च सेन्द्रान्देवान्विजिग्ये ।
1.191.m: 222 Having killed the messenger of the Lord of Wealth who said, "Do not commit insolence; your destruction is being contemplated by the gods," and having seized his Puṣpaka aerial car, Rāvaṇa went to Kailāsa; when Rāvaṇa laughed aloud seeing Nandin in the form of a monkey, Nandikeśvara uttered a curse, saying, "Your destruction shall be caused by monkeys born in the family of the patriarch Pulaha"; when Rāvaṇa wished to carry Hara together with Kailāsa to Laṅkā, Hara, pleased by the spontaneous embrace of Umā caused by the agitation of the mountain's shaking, gave him the name Rāvaṇa; and then Rāvaṇa, having conquered the King of Dharma together with the noose of Time, Yama, and the hosts of the ancestors in Saṃyaminī, approached to fight with Sūrya; Brahmā held back Sūrya, and Rāvaṇa conquered the gods led by Indra.

1.191.s: 223 rāvaṇaḥ pātāle kālakhañjādidaityānvijitya brahmānurodhena nivātakavacaiḥ saha sakhyañcakāra, nāgānsasutaṃ varuṇañca jitvā kiṣkindhāyāṃ yuddhārthaṃ vālinaṃ papraccha, tāreṇa dundubhighātanaṃ sugrīvasya niṣkāsanaṃ hanūmatpauruṣañca varṇitam ..
1.191.d: 223 रावणः पाताले कालखञ्जादिदैत्यान्विजित्य ब्रह्मानुरोधेन निवातकवचैः सह सख्यञ्चकार, नागान्ससुतं वरुणञ्च जित्वा किष्किन्धायां युद्धार्थं वालिनं पप्रच्छ, तारेण दुन्दुभिघातनं सुग्रीवस्य निष्कासनं हनूमत्पौरुषञ्च वर्णितम् ॥
1.191.m: 223 In Pātāla, having conquered the daityas such as the Kālakhañjas, Rāvaṇa made an alliance with the Nivātakavacas at the request of Brahmā; having defeated the nāgas and Varuṇa along with his son, he asked Vālin in Kiṣkindhā for battle; the slaying of Dundubhi, the banishment of Sugrīva, and the heroism of Hanūmat are described by Tāra.
Thereafter the text is fragmentary; the remainder of this chapter and the two hundred and twenty-fourth chapter are not available.
225 The hymn of praise to Gaṇeśa performed by Śaṅkara at the conclusion of the burning of Tripura.

1.191.s: 226 andhakāsurasamare tadastrasañjātānekāndhakakhinnena śambhunā māheśvaryādimātṝḥ sṛṣṭvāpi yadā nāndhakāsṛkkṣayastadā tattuṣṭavāsudevasṛṣṭaśuṣkarevatīpītarudhirā andhakāḥ kṣayaṃ prāpuḥ mūlāndhakaṃ tatprārthanayā śivo gaṇeśatvaṃ svasāmīpyañca dadau tato mātṝṇāmupadrave vṛddhe rudrasmṛtanṛharirvāgīśvaryādīḥ sasarja, tattejobhītāḥ pūrvamātaraḥ nṛsiṃhaṃ śaraṇaṃ jagmuḥ sa ca tatpūjakānāmabhīṣṭasiddhiṃ svīkṛtya tāḥ pūjyā vyadhatta
1.191.d: 226 अन्धकासुरसमरे तदस्त्रसञ्जातानेकान्धकखिन्नेन शम्भुना माहेश्वर्यादिमातॄः सृष्ट्वापि यदा नान्धकासृक्क्षयस्तदा तत्तुष्टवासुदेवसृष्टशुष्करेवतीपीतरुधिरा अन्धकाः क्षयं प्रापुः मूलान्धकं तत्प्रार्थनया शिवो गणेशत्वं स्वसामीप्यञ्च ददौ ततो मातॄणामुपद्रवे वृद्धे रुद्रस्मृतनृहरिर्वागीश्वर्यादीः ससर्ज, तत्तेजोभीताः पूर्वमातरः नृसिंहं शरणं जग्मुः स च तत्पूजकानामभीष्टसिद्धिं स्वीकृत्य ताः पूज्या व्यधत्त
1.191.m: 226 In the battle with the asura Andhaka, when Śambhu, afflicted by the numerous Andhakas born from his weapon, created the Mothers such as Māheśvarī, yet the blood of Andhaka was not depleted, then the Andhakas met destruction when their blood was drunk by Śuṣkarevatī, who was created by Vāsudeva who was pleased with him; upon his request, Śiva granted the original Andhaka the status of a Gaṇeśa and proximity to himself; then, when the affliction caused by the Mothers grew, Rudra remembered Nṛhari, who created Vāgīśvarī and the others; frightened by their brilliance, the former Mothers took refuge in Nṛsiṃha, who, granting the attainment of desired ends for their worshippers, rendered them worthy of worship.
227 The description of the bath, ointment, incense, offerings, the five products of the cow, and so forth, which destroy the afflictions caused by the Mothers.

1.191.s: 228 parasparaspardhamānaharagauryo rahasyakrīḍāyāmanyatarasyāviratatayā vahnestatra kapotarūpeṇa praveśe śaṅkararetaścyutaṃ vahnerāsyamaviśacchaśāpa ca girijādevānsvasvabhāryāsu naiva putrāṃllabhadhvamiti, atyugraṃ hi śivareto bahirujjagāra gaṅgā ca taddadhāra, gaṅgāpyasahyaṃ tattejaḥ śvete girau tatyāja, ṣaṭkṛttikāśca taddadhuḥ śaṅkarasūnuḥ ṣaḍānano bhūtvā tāsāṃ stanānpapau tatpayovṛddhaśca kṛttikācandrayoge vahniguhakṛttikāvaruṇapūjākarttarabhimateṣṭasiddhiṃ varaṃ dadau
1.191.d: 228 परस्परस्पर्धमानहरगौर्यो रहस्यक्रीडायामन्यतरस्याविरततया वह्नेस्तत्र कपोतरूपेण प्रवेशे शङ्कररेतश्च्युतं वह्नेरास्यमविशच्छशाप च गिरिजादेवान्स्वस्वभार्यासु नैव पुत्रांल्लभध्वमिति, अत्युग्रं हि शिवरेतो बहिरुज्जगार गङ्गा च तद्दधार, गङ्गाप्यसह्यं तत्तेजः श्वेते गिरौ तत्याज, षट्कृत्तिकाश्च तद्दधुः शङ्करसूनुः षडाननो भूत्वा तासां स्तनान्पपौ तत्पयोवृद्धश्च कृत्तिकाचन्द्रयोगे वह्निगुहकृत्तिकावरुणपूजाकर्त्तरभिमतेष्टसिद्धिं वरं ददौ
1.191.m: 228 While Hara and Gaurī were engaged in secret sport competing with each other, because neither of them ceased, Agni entered there in the form of a dove; Śaṅkara’s semen dropped and entered the mouth of Agni; and Girijā cursed the gods, saying, “You shall never obtain sons in your own wives.” Indeed, Agni spewed out the extremely fierce semen of Śiva, and Gaṅgā held it; Gaṅgā too, unable to bear that splendour, cast it upon the Śveta mountain; and the six Kṛttikās took it up; the son of Śaṅkara, becoming six-faced, drank their breasts, and grown on their milk, he granted the boon of the attainment of desired wishes to anyone who worships Agni, Guha, the Kṛttikās, and Varuṇa during the conjunction of the Kṛttikās and the moon.

1.191.s: 229 tvattejo'sahantyā mayā śvetagirau tvaṃ tyakta iti kathayantīṃ gaṅgāṃ kārtikeyo'kṣayatṛtīyāyāṃ kutrāpi snānakarturgaṅgāsnānaphalaprāptiṃ dānādeścākṣayaphalatāñcakāra
1.191.d: 229 त्वत्तेजोऽसहन्त्या मया श्वेतगिरौ त्वं त्यक्त इति कथयन्तीं गङ्गां कार्तिकेयोऽक्षयतृतीयायां कुत्रापि स्नानकर्तुर्गङ्गास्नानफलप्राप्तिं दानादेश्चाक्षयफलताञ्चकार
1.191.m: 229 When Gaṅgā said, “Unable to bear your splendour, I abandoned you on the Śveta mountain,” Kārttikeya granted that anyone who bathes anywhere on Akṣayatṛtīyā obtains the fruit of bathing in the Gaṅgā, and that gifts and the like yield imperishable fruit.

1.191.s: 230 śvetagirāvapūrvasattvaṃ śrutvā devadaityādibhirāmantrya śakrastannāśāya matiṃ cakre, skandastvaparāngrahānnirmāya sarvāstānnirvīryām̐ñcakre, nāstikādibhyastadvṛttimapi svīcakre
1.191.d: 230 श्वेतगिरावपूर्वसत्त्वं श्रुत्वा देवदैत्यादिभिरामन्त्र्य शक्रस्तन्नाशाय मतिं चक्रे, स्कन्दस्त्वपरान्ग्रहान्निर्माय सर्वास्तान्निर्वीर्याम्̐ञ्चक्रे, नास्तिकादिभ्यस्तद्वृत्तिमपि स्वीचक्रे
1.191.m: 230 Hearing of the unprecedented being on the Śveta mountain, Śakra, having conferred with the gods, daityas, and others, resolved to destroy it; but Skanda, having created other grahas, rendered all of them powerless, and he accepted their livelihood from atheists and the like.
231 The marks of one seized by a graha.
232 Rites beginning with anointing that remove the afflictions of the nine grahas; the grahas are always favourable to one who worships cows, twice-born people, and the gods.
233 The praise of Kārttikeya spoken by Śakra, and the slaying of Mahiṣāsura performed by Kārttikeya.

1.191.s: 234 devairyajñe śaṅkarabhāge'kalpite śivastānvitrāsayāmāsa puroḍāśamattvā pūṣṇo dantānbhagasya vāmanayanañcānāśayat, yajño naranārāyaṇāśramamadravadviṣṇuśaraṇamagamaddharastamanujagrāha ca
1.191.d: 234 देवैर्यज्ञे शङ्करभागेऽकल्पिते शिवस्तान्वित्रासयामास पुरोडाशमत्त्वा पूष्णो दन्तान्भगस्य वामनयनञ्चानाशयत्, यज्ञो नरनारायणाश्रममद्रवद्विष्णुशरणमगमद्धरस्तमनुजग्राह च
1.191.m: 234 When the gods did not assign a share to Śaṅkara in the sacrifice, Śiva terrified them: eating the sacrificial cake, he destroyed the teeth of Pūṣan and the left eye of Bhaga; the sacrifice fled to the hermitage of Nara and Nārāyaṇa and sought refuge with Viṣṇu, and Hara showed it favour.

1.191.s: 235 gaṅgādvāre dakṣayajñe śaṅkarānāhvānādvīrabhadrabhadrakālībhyāṃ dakṣayajñavidhvaṃsaḥ, vīrabhadropadeśātstutabhadrakarṇeśvaro dakṣo'śvamedhasahasraphalaṃ lebhe . haradvāre kuśāvartāditīrthapañcakaprāśastyam
1.191.d: 235 गङ्गाद्वारे दक्षयज्ञे शङ्करानाह्वानाद्वीरभद्रभद्रकालीभ्यां दक्षयज्ञविध्वंसः, वीरभद्रोपदेशात्स्तुतभद्रकर्णेश्वरो दक्षोऽश्वमेधसहस्रफलं लेभे । हरद्वारे कुशावर्तादितीर्थपञ्चकप्राशस्त्यम्
1.191.m: 235 At Gaṅgādvāra, because Śaṅkara was not invited to Dakṣa’s sacrifice, the destruction of Dakṣa’s sacrifice by Vīrabhadra and Bhadrakālī; through the instruction of Vīrabhadra, Dakṣa praised Bhadrakarṇeśvara and obtained the fruit of a thousand horse-sacrifices. The excellence of the five holy bathing-places beginning with Kuśāvarta at Haradvāra.

1.191.s: 236 śambhuṃ pūjayati śvetarṣau mūrtimān kālastasyāyuṣaḥ pūrṇatvāttamānetuṃ taddeśamāgataḥ, kṛtavaiṣṇavakavacarakṣaḥ śambhuḥ kālaṃ bhasmasādakarot ....
1.191.d: 236 शम्भुं पूजयति श्वेतर्षौ मूर्तिमान् कालस्तस्यायुषः पूर्णत्वात्तमानेतुं तद्देशमागतः, कृतवैष्णवकवचरक्षः शम्भुः कालं भस्मसादकरोत् ॥॥
1.191.m: 236 While the sage Śveta was worshipping Śambhu, embodied Kāla, because his lifespan was complete, arrived at that place to take him; having formed the protection of the Vaiṣṇava armour, Śambhu reduced Kāla to ashes.
237 The proclamation of the armour of Nārāyaṇa.

1.191.s:
238 svapratibhaṭajijñāsayā balisadmani gate rāvaṇe sauhārdāttvadbaddhāraṃ viṣṇuṃ jeṣyāmīti bruvāṇe tatrasthamatkaṭakamānīyātropaviśeti balinoktaḥ sa
sarvayatnādapi na śaśāka kuṇḍalamānetum, etābhyāṃ ca kuṇḍalābhyāṃ hiraṇyakaśipurmatprapitāmaho'śobhata yamayaṃ matkuṇaprāyamamardayat mṛṣā
tajjaye tavāśeti
1.191.d:
238 स्वप्रतिभटजिज्ञासया बलिसद्मनि गते रावणे सौहार्दात्त्वद्बद्धारं विष्णुं जेष्यामीति ब्रुवाणे तत्रस्थमत्कटकमानीयात्रोपविशेति बलिनोक्तः स
सर्वयत्नादपि न शशाक कुण्डलमानेतुम्, एताभ्यां च कुण्डलाभ्यां हिरण्यकशिपुर्मत्प्रपितामहोऽशोभत यमयं मत्कुणप्रायममर्दयत् मृषा
तज्जये तवाशेति
1.191.m: 238 When Rāvaṇa went to the abode of Bali out of curiosity about an opponent for himself, saying out of friendship, “I shall conquer Viṣṇu who bound you,” he was told by Bali, “Bring here my bracelet lying over there and sit down”; even with all his effort he could not bring [even] an earring; and [Bali said], “With these two earrings my great-grandfather Hiraṇyakaśipu shone, whom this [Viṣṇu] crushed like a bedbug; your hope to conquer him is in vain.”
239 Rāvaṇa’s vision of Viṣṇu’s cosmic form.
240 The description of spring in Ayodhyā.
241 The description of summer in Ayodhyā.

1.191.s: 242 sādhukaṇṭakaṃ madhudaityaṃ jahati cyavanapuraḥsarayamunātīrthasthamunivṛnda āgate sasainyasya śatrughnasya rāmājñayā tadvadhāya gamanam
1.191.d: 242 साधुकण्टकं मधुदैत्यं जहति च्यवनपुरःसरयमुनातीर्थस्थमुनिवृन्द आगते ससैन्यस्य शत्रुघ्नस्य रामाज्ञया तद्वधाय गमनम्
1.191.m: 242 When a host of sages dwelling on the bank of the Yamunā, led by Cyavana, arrived [complaining] that the Madhu daitya was afflicting the virtuous, the departure of Śatrughna with his army, by order of Rāma, to slay him.
243 The description of the rainy season.
244 The description of autumn in the instruction of Rāma to Śatrughna.
245 The description of early winter in the instruction on duties in early winter given by Rāma to Śatrughna.
246 The description of late winter in Rāma’s instruction to Śatrughna.

1.191.s: 247 śrīvaśiṣṭharāmādipādāvabhivādya śatrughno madhurājigamiṣayā prathamaṃ vālmīkyāśramaṃ prāpa, śatrughnakṛtalavaṇavadhānantaraṃ suprītadevecchayā śatrughnena mathurānirmāṇam
1.191.d: 247 श्रीवशिष्ठरामादिपादावभिवाद्य शत्रुघ्नो मधुराजिगमिषया प्रथमं वाल्मीक्याश्रमं प्राप, शत्रुघ्नकृतलवणवधानन्तरं सुप्रीतदेवेच्छया शत्रुघ्नेन मथुरानिर्माणम्
1.191.m: 247 Having bowed to the feet of the venerable Vasiṣṭha, Rāma, and the others, Śatrughna, wishing to go to Madhurā, first reached the hermitage of Vālmīki; after the slaying of Lavaṇa by Śatrughna, the construction of Mathurā by Śatrughna in accordance with the wish of the well-pleased gods.
248 In the context of describing the lineage of Pulaha, the description of the creation of deer and the like through Pulaha by the daughters beginning with Mṛgā and Mṛgamandā.

1.191.s: 249 oṣadhidvijātinakṣatrayajñatapasāṃ candraṃ, sarvaprajāpatīnāṃ dakṣaṃ, sarvendriyāṇāṃ manasaṃ, surastrīṇāṃ manmathamityādi pratisamūhe rājakīrtanam
1.191.d: 249 ओषधिद्विजातिनक्षत्रयज्ञतपसां चन्द्रं, सर्वप्रजापतीनां दक्षं, सर्वेन्द्रियाणां मनसं, सुरस्त्रीणां मन्मथमित्यादि प्रतिसमूहे राजकीर्तनम्
1.191.m: 249 The proclamation of kings over each group: the Moon over medicinal herbs, the twice-born, constellations, sacrifices, and austerities; Dakṣa over all progenitors; the mind over all sense-faculties; Manmatha over celestial women; and so forth.
250 Brahmā consecrated Śakra, the son of Kaśyapa, in the sovereignty over the gods.
251 The eight families and the eight forests of elephants.
252 The description of the origin of monkeys and the defeat of the elephants by them.
253 The description of the battle between elephants and monkeys.

1.191.s: 254 śvo bharatena saha yoddhavyamadya sarverviśrāmasukhamanubhūyāvaśyakaṃ kṛtvā śva āgantavyamiti śailūṣanirdeśaḥ
1.191.d: 254 श्वो भरतेन सह योद्धव्यमद्य सर्वेर्विश्रामसुखमनुभूयावश्यकं कृत्वा श्व आगन्तव्यमिति शैलूषनिर्देशः
1.191.m: 254 Śailūṣa’s command: “Tomorrow we must fight with Bharata; today, all should enjoy the comfort of rest, attend to necessities, and arrive tomorrow.”
255 The description of women separated from their lovers in Ayodhyā.
256 The description of women whose husbands are abroad in Ayodhyā.
257 The description of the soldiers’ nocturnal amusement in Bharata’s army.
258 The description of the army of the Gandharvas preparing for battle.
259 The march of Bharata’s army.
260 The description of the tumultuous battle between the armies of Bharata and the Gandharvas.
261 The description of the fierce battle between Bharata and King Śailūṣa.
262 The description of the third day’s battle of Bharata with the Gandharvas.
263 The account of the battle on the fourth day.
264 The news of the battle on the fifth day.

1.191.s: 265 śailūṣe hatarathe bharate ca tathāvidhe bhīṣaṇayuddhānantaraṃ ṣaṣṭhadivasayuddhaviratiḥ
1.191.d: 265 शैलूषे हतरथे भरते च तथाविधे भीषणयुद्धानन्तरं षष्ठदिवसयुद्धविरतिः
1.191.m: 265 When Śailūṣa had his chariot destroyed, and Bharata was in the same condition, after a terrifying battle, the cessation of fighting on the sixth day.

1.191.s: 266 nānāmāyāyuddhe bharatavihitaśailūṣavadhe sañjāte śailūṣaputrādhiṣṭhitatrikoṭigandharvasainyānāmapi nāśe śakrasya bharatasamīpaṃ varadānārthaṃ gamanam, sindhukūlayoḥ puraddhaye tvatputrayo rājye sta ityabhidhāya svargagamanañca, bharataṃ sabhājāyitvā citrarathasyāpi nākaprayāṇam
1.191.d: 266 नानामायायुद्धे भरतविहितशैलूषवधे सञ्जाते शैलूषपुत्राधिष्ठितत्रिकोटिगन्धर्वसैन्यानामपि नाशे शक्रस्य भरतसमीपं वरदानार्थं गमनम्, सिन्धुकूलयोः पुरद्धये त्वत्पुत्रयो राज्ये स्त इत्यभिधाय स्वर्गगमनञ्च, भरतं सभाजायित्वा चित्ररथस्यापि नाकप्रयाणम्
1.191.m: 266 When, in a battle of diverse sorceries, the slaying of Śailūṣa was accomplished by Bharata, and the army of thirty million Gandharvas commanded by Śailūṣa’s sons was also destroyed, Śakra’s arrival before Bharata to grant a boon; his departure to heaven after saying, “Let the two cities on the banks of the Sindhu be the kingdoms of your two sons”; and, having honoured Bharata, Citraratha’s departure to heaven as well.
267 As Bharata and Yudhājit were returning to their camp, the description of the battlefield given by Yudhājit.
268 The heart-rending lamentation of the Gandharva women on seeing the lifeless Gandharvas on the battlefield.
269 Bharata, returned from the battle, having won an audience with Rāma, offering the jewels of the conquered Gandharvas to Rāma.
Thus ends the first book.

श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
वज्र उवाच ॥

यच्छ्रुत्वा वेद्मि चात्मानं ब्रह्मन्विगतकल्मषम् ॥1 ॥
2.1.m:
2.1
Homage to the venerable Gaṇeśa.
Vajra said:
At first, the victory of Bharata was told to me by your lordship;
hearing which, O brahmin, I know myself to be freed from taint.

sukhaśrāvyaśca hṛdyaśca kathāsārastu bhārgava ..
kathāśca vividhāḥ proktāstatprasaṅgāttvayānagha .. 2 ..

सुखश्राव्यश्च हृद्यश्च कथासारस्तु भार्गव ॥
कथाश्च विविधाः प्रोक्तास्तत्प्रसङ्गात्त्वयानघ ॥ 2 ॥
2.1.m:
Pleasant to hear and delightful is the essence of the story, O descendant of Bhṛgu;
and various tales have been recounted by you in that connection, O sinless one,

rasavatyaśca dharmajña sarvapāpakṣayaṅkarāḥ ..
yāstā brahmanprasaṅgena mayāpahṛtacetasā .. 3 ..

रसवत्यश्च धर्मज्ञ सर्वपापक्षयङ्कराः ॥
यास्ता ब्रह्मन्प्रसङ्गेन मयापहृतचेतसा ॥ 3 ॥
2.1.m:
full of flavour, O knower of dharma, and bringing about the destruction of all sins.
Those [tales], O brahmin, which in that context by me whose heart was captivated

prastutāstāḥ kathāstyaktāstā eva kathasva me ..
bhagavansarvadharmajña pratyakṣāmaladarthana ..
kathānāṃ tu prasaṅgena prastutā yāḥ kathāḥ purā ..4..

प्रस्तुतास्ताः कथास्त्यक्तास्ता एव कथस्व मे ॥
भगवन्सर्वधर्मज्ञ प्रत्यक्षामलदर्थन ॥
कथानां तु प्रसङ्गेन प्रस्तुता याः कथाः पुरा ॥4॥
2.1.m: Those stories that were commenced were set aside; tell me those very [stories]. / O venerable one, knower of all dharmas, whose sight is pure and direct, / those stories that were commenced before in the course of the narrations,

sudūramantarībhūtvā rāmasya viditātmanaḥ ..
tā eva śrotumicchāmi tvatto bhṛgukulodvaha ..5..

ता एव श्रोतुमिच्छामि त्वत्तो भृगुकुलोद्वह ॥5॥
2.1.m: having been interrupted for so long, of Rāma whose self is known, / those very [stories] I wish to hear from you, O scion of Bhṛgu's lineage.

2.1.s:
lokaṃ vāruṇamāsādya rāmo bhṛgukulodvahaḥ ..
śrutavāndevadeveśānkinnu bhūyaḥ pracetasaḥ ..6..

लोकं वारुणमासाद्य रामो भृगुकुलोद्वहः ॥
श्रुतवान्देवदेवेशान्किन्नु भूयः प्रचेतसः ॥6॥
2.1.m: Having reached the world of Varuṇa, Rāma, scion of Bhṛgu's lineage, / what further did he hear from Pracetas, the lord of gods and lords?

2.1.s:
etanme sarvamācakṣva tatra me saṃśayo mahān ..
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
kālasya saṃkhyāṃ tāṃ śrutvā rāmaproktāṃ pracetasā .. 7 ..
2.1.d:
एतन्मे सर्वमाचक्ष्व तत्र मे संशयो महान् ॥
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
कालस्य संख्यां तां श्रुत्वा रामप्रोक्तां प्रचेतसा ॥ 7 ॥
2.1.m: Tell me all this; in that matter my doubt is great. / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having heard that reckoning of time told to Rāma by Pracetas,

2.1.s:
papraccha varuṇaṃ devaṃ rājadharmānataḥ param ..
pṛṣṭastu jāmadagnyena rāmaṃ prāha jaleśvaraḥ..8..
2.1.d:
पप्रच्छ वरुणं देवं राजधर्मानतः परम् ॥

रामेण पृष्टो वरुणस्य पुत्रो जगाद धर्मान्नृपसत्तमानाम् ॥

2.2
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
सुखासीनो नरश्रेष्ठः पुष्करस्य निवेशने ॥
पप्रच्छ पुष्करं रामो धर्मनित्यो जितेन्द्रियः ॥ 1 ॥
राम उवाच ॥
राष्ट्रस्य किं कृत्यतमं तन्माचक्ष्व पृच्छतः ॥
आदावेव महाभाग यादोगणनृपात्मज ॥ 2 ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
राष्ट्रस्य कृत्यं धर्मज्ञ राज्ञ एवाभिषेचनम् ॥
अनिन्द्रमबलं राष्ट्रं दस्यवोऽभिभवन्त्युत ॥ 3 ॥
अराजकेषु राष्ट्रेषु धर्मावस्था न विद्यते ॥
वर्णानामाश्रमाणां च व्यवस्थानं च भार्गव ॥ 4 ।
अराजकेषु राष्ट्रेषु नैव कन्या प्रदीयते ॥
विद्यते मम ता नैव तथा वित्तेषु कस्यचित् ॥ 5 ॥
स्वात्म्यो न्यायः प्रवर्तेत विश्वलोपस्तथैव च ॥
लोके न कश्चिद्विद्येत गुरोर्वचनकारकः ॥ 6 ॥।
2.1.m:
Questioned by Rāma, the son of Varuṇa spoke of the duties of the best of kings, / full of substance and of great import, for the protection of all the world on earth, O moon among kings.
2.2 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Seated comfortably in Puṣkara's dwelling, the best among men, / Rāma, constant in dharma and with senses conquered, questioned Puṣkara.
Rāma said: / "What is the most urgent duty of a kingdom? Tell that to me as I ask, / at the very beginning, O fortunate one, O son of the king of aquatic creatures."
Puṣkara said: / "The duty of a kingdom, O knower of dharma, is indeed the consecration of a king. / A kingless, powerless kingdom the robbers overcome.
In kingless kingdoms, no order of dharma exists, / nor the proper maintenance of the classes and life-stages, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
In kingless kingdoms, a maiden is not given in marriage at all; / no sense of 'this is mine' exists in property for anyone.
The law of self-interest would prevail, as well as universal plunder; / no one in the world would be found carrying out the words of a guru.

2.1.d:
नाधीयीरम्̐स्त्रयीं विद्यां त्रयो वर्णा द्विजातयः ॥
देवानां यजनं न स्यादनावृष्टिस्ततो भवेत् ॥ 7 ॥
नृलोकसुरलोकौ च स्यातां संशयितावुभौ ॥।
जनमारी भवेद्घोरा यदि राजा न पालयेत् ॥8॥
प्रजानां रक्षणार्थाय विष्णुतेजोपबृंहितः ॥
मानुष्ये जायते राजा देवसत्त्ववपुर्धरः ॥ 9 ॥
यस्मिन्प्रसन्ने देवस्य प्रसादस्तूपजायते ॥
यस्मिन्क्रुद्धे जनस्यास्य क्रोधः समुपजायते ॥ 10 ॥
महद्भिः पुण्यसम्भारैः पार्थिवो राम जायते ॥
यस्यैकस्य जगत्सर्वं वचने राम तिष्ठति ॥ 11 ॥
चातुर्वर्ण्यं स्वधर्मस्थं तेषु देशेषु जायते ॥
येषु देशेषु राजेन्द्र राजा भवति धार्मिकः ॥ 12 ॥
(मारकं न च दुर्भिक्षं नाग्निचौरभयं तथा ॥
न च व्यालभयं तेषां येषां धर्मपरो नृपः) ॥ 13 ॥
2.1.m:
The three twice-born classes would not study the threefold science; / there would be no sacrificing to the gods, and drought would result therefrom.
Both the world of mortals and the world of the gods would be placed in jeopardy; / a dreadful plague would arise if the king did not protect.
For the protection of the subjects, augmented by the splendour of Viṣṇu, / the king is born in human form, bearing a body of divine essence,
in whose pleasure the grace of the god arises, / and in whose anger the wrath of this people arises.
By vast accumulations of merit a king is born, O Rāma, / at whose sole command the entire world abides, O Rāma.
The four classes stand firm in their own dharma in those lands / in which, O best of kings, the king is righteous.
(Neither pestilence, nor famine, nor danger from fire and thieves, / nor danger from wild beasts exists for those who have a king devoted to dharma.)

2.1.m: First one should secure a king, then a wife, then wealth. / Under a bad king, whence a wife, whence wealth for this people?

2.1.m: Therefore, by every effort, a king who is righteous and true to his promise / must be established by the former leaders of the realm after testing.

पुष्कर उवाच ॥
सर्वलक्षणलक्षण्यो विनीतः प्रियदर्शनः ॥
अदीर्घसूत्री धर्मात्मा जितक्रोधो जितेन्द्रियः ॥ 1 ॥
स्थूललक्षो महोत्साहः स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषकः ॥
सुरूपः कुलसंपन्नः क्षिप्रकारी महाबलः ॥ 2 ॥
ब्रह्मण्यश्चाविसंवादी दृढभक्तिः प्रियंवदः ॥
अलोलुपस्संयतवाग्गंभीरः प्रियदर्शनः ॥ ॥ 3 ॥
नातिदण्डो न निर्दण्डः चारचक्षुरजिह्मगः ॥
व्यवहारे समः प्राप्ते पुत्रस्य रिपुणा सह ॥ 4 ॥

मन्त्रिसांवत्सराधीनः समरेष्वनिवर्तकः ॥

2.1.m:
For those whose king on earth is constant in dharma, there is no fear whatsoever in the world; / therefore, with effort, O lord of men, a disciplined king must be made by the foremost of the kingdom.
2.3 / Puṣkara said: / Characterised by all auspicious marks, disciplined, pleasant to look upon, / not given to procrastination, righteous, his anger conquered, his senses subdued,
bountiful, of great energy, speaking with a prior smile, / handsome, born of noble family, swift to act, of great strength,
devoted to brahmins, not contentious, of firm devotion, pleasant of speech, / free from greed, restrained of speech, profound, pleasant to look upon,
neither punishing excessively nor failing to punish, having spies for eyes, upright in conduct, / impartial in legal proceedings when a son comes [into conflict] with an enemy,
skilled through practice in chariot, elephant, horse, bow, and exercise, / devoted to fasting and austerity, performing sacrifices, dear to his elders,
reliant on ministers and astrologers, unyielding in battles, / knowing the right time, grateful, and knowing the distinctions among men,

2.1.m:
always honouring what is worthy of honour, and likewise punishing what is worthy of punishment, / applying the six measures of policy, and similarly endowed with the [three] powers—
adorned with these and many other qualities, both mentioned and unmentioned, / a ruler of the earth, of undiscouraged spirit, should be appointed by the chiefs of the realm together, according to rule, for the realm's protection.
2.4 / Puṣkara said: / Possessing such a multitude of qualities, a kṣatriya born of noble lineage, / the foremost of the realm, having assembled, should choose as king.
And chosen by them, the king, with conquered senses, should take the vow: / "I shall protect all of you who abide in dharma; of this there is no doubt."
Having taken the vow, desiring the kingdom, for the happiness of this entire world, / the king should choose an excellent brahmin astrologer,
characterised by all auspicious marks, disciplined, pleasant to look upon, / handsome, suitably attired, and always energetic in appearance,
One who speaks without dejection, resolute, steadfast in dharma, with subdued senses, / without deformed limbs, without redundant limbs, and having mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas;

चतुःषष्ट्यङ्गतत्त्वज्ञमूहापोहविशारदम् ॥
भूतभव्यभविष्यज्ञं गणितज्ञं विशेषतः ॥ 6 ॥
विचन्द्रा शर्वरी यद्वन्मुकुटं च च्युतोपलम् ॥
गणितेन तथा हीनं ज्योतिषं नृपसत्तम ॥ 7 ॥
आस्तिकं श्रद्दधानं च अनुकूलं महीपतेः ॥
सांवत्सरं नृपो गत्वा वरयेत्प्रयतः शुचिः ॥ 8 ॥
येनाभिषिक्तो नृपतिर्विनष्टस्तु नराधिप ॥
सांवत्सरं न तं विद्वान्वरयेन्नृपसत्तम॥ 9 ॥
न हीनाङ्गं न वाचालं न च निष्प्रतिभं नृपः ॥
कुवेशमलिनं मुण्डं नास्तिकं पापनिश्चयम् ॥ 10 ॥
भिन्नवृत्तिं च वरयेद्वरयेत्सद्गुणं सदा ॥
वरयित्वा तु वक्तव्याः स्वयमेव महीभुजा ॥ 11 ॥
यथैवाग्निमुखा देवास्तथा राजमुखाः प्रजाः ॥
यथैवाग्निमुखा मन्त्रा राज्ञां सांवत्सरास्तथा ॥ 12 ॥
त्वं मे माता पिता चैव देशिकश्च गुरुस्तथा ॥
दैवं पुरुषकारश्च ज्ञातव्यौ सततं त्वया ॥ 13 ॥
2.1.m:
knowing the truth of the sixty-four branches, skilled in reasoning and deduction, / knowing the past, present, and future, and especially skilled in mathematics.
Just as a night is without a moon, or a crown has lost its jewels, / even so is astrology devoid of mathematics, O best of kings.
An orthodox believer, faithful, and well-disposed to the king— / going to such an astrologer, the king, restrained and pure, should select him.
An astrologer consecrated by whom a king has perished, O ruler of men, / a wise man should not select, O best of kings.
Nor one of defective limbs, nor a chatterer, nor one devoid of wit, / nor one poorly clad, filthy, shaven-headed, an atheist, or resolved on evil;
nor should he select one of corrupted conduct; he should always select one with virtuous qualities. / Having selected him, he must be spoken to by the king himself:
‘Just as the gods have fire for their mouth, so subjects have the king for their mouth; / just as mantras have fire for their mouth, so kings have astrologers.’
‘You are indeed my mother, my father, my spiritual guide, and my teacher; / fate and human effort must always be examined by you.’

पौरुषेण पदं कार्यं समरं च तथा मया ॥
स चेत्तदभिमन्येत पार्थिवस्य महागुणम् ॥ 15 ॥

2.1.m:
‘O knower of the impartial dharma, hail to you! For the kingdom is common to us both; / auspicious fate must indeed be brought forth by you alone for me, O best of men.’
‘Through human effort, a step must be taken and battle fought by me.’ / If he thus esteems the sovereign’s great virtue,
or swiftly, through virtue and fault and through wisdom, discerning human beings’ / affliction by fate in battle and understanding human effort,

तेनोद्दिष्टौ तु वरयेद्राजा मन्त्रिपुरोहितौ ॥ 17 ॥

2.1.m: And the best of kings should select the chief queen designated by him. / Then that astrologer should prepare the provisions for his coronation.

2.1.m: Those that are superior in quality, which I have spoken of elsewhere, should not be used.

न तत्र नागाः सुभृता न योधा राज्ञो न माता न पिता न बन्धुः ॥
यत्रास्य साध्यं भवतीह विद्वान्सांवत्सरो धर्मविदः प्रमत्तः ॥ 23 ॥
2.5
राम उवाच ॥
राज्ञा पुरोहितः कार्यस्तथा मन्त्री च कीदृशः ॥
महिषी च तथा ज्येष्ठा तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः ॥ ॥ 1 ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
अव्यङ्गं लक्षणोपेतमनुकूलं प्रियंवदम् ॥
अथर्ववेदविद्वांसं यजुर्वेदविशारदम् ॥ 2 ॥
द्विवेदं ब्राह्मणं राजा पुरोहितमथर्वणम् ॥
पञ्चकल्पविधानज्ञं वरयेत सुदर्शनम् ॥3॥
नक्षत्रकल्पो वैतानस्तृतीयः संहिताविधिः ॥
चतुर्थोङ्गिरसां कल्पः शान्तिकल्पस्तु पञ्चमः ॥4॥
पञ्चकल्पविधानज्ञमाचार्यं प्राप्य भूपतिः ॥
सर्वोत्पातप्रशान्तात्मा भुनक्ति वसुधां चिरम् ॥5॥
स च राज्ञस्तथा कुर्यान्नित्यं कर्म सदैव तु ॥
नैमित्तिकं तथा काम्यं दैवज्ञवचने रतः ॥6॥
2.1.m:
Neither elephants well cared for nor warriors help him, nor the king’s mother, father, or kin, / where the astrologer of him who knows dharma becomes heedless in what must be accomplished here, O wise one.
2.5 / Rāma said: / What kind of royal priest should be appointed by the king, and what kind of minister, / and likewise what kind of chief queen? Tell that to me as I ask.
Puṣkara said: / Unmaimed, endowed with auspicious marks, agreeable, pleasant of speech, / learned in the Atharvaveda, and skilled in the Yajurveda;
the king should select a handsome brahmin priest learned in two Vedas, / adhering to the Atharvaveda, knowing the procedures of the five rituals.
The Nakṣatrakalpa, the Vaitāna, the third is the Saṃhitāvidhi, / the fourth is the ritual of the Aṅgirases, and the Śāntikalpa is the fifth.
Having obtained a teacher knowing the rules of the five rituals, / the king, with all portents pacified within him, enjoys the earth for a long time.
And he should always perform the king’s daily rites, / as well as occasional and optional rites, intent upon the astrologer’s word.

2.1.d:
न त्याज्यस्तु भवेद्राजा दैवज्ञेन पुरोधसा ॥
पतितस्तु भवेत्त्याज्यो नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥7॥
तथैव पतितौ राम न त्याज्यौ तौ महीभुजा ॥
तयोस्त्यागेन राजेन्द्र राज्यभ्रंशो विनिर्दिशेत ॥ 8 ॥
दुर्गतिः परलोके च बहुकालमसंशयम् ॥
सांवत्सरविरुद्धस्तु त्याज्यो राज्ञा पुरोहितः ॥
पुरोहितोऽन्यथा राज्ञो यथा माता यथा पिता ॥
अनिष्टमस्य व्यसनं हन्याद्दैवोपघातजम् ॥ 10 ॥
ब्राह्मणो निष्कृतिस्तस्य कुत्र शक्या महीभुजा ॥
यावन्न राज्ञा विद्वांसौ सांवत्सरपुरोहितौ ॥ 11 ॥
वृत्तिच्छेदे तयो राज्ञः कुलं त्रिपुरुषं व्रजेत् ॥
नरकं वर्जयेत्तस्माद्वृतच्छेदं तयोः सदा ॥ 12 ॥
स्थावरेण विभागश्च तयोः कार्यो विशेषतः ॥
अनुरूपेण धर्मज्ञ सांवत्सरपुरोहितौ ॥ 13 ॥
2.1.m:
The king should not be abandoned by the astrologer and the royal priest; / but if fallen, he should be abandoned; there is no hesitation in this matter.
Likewise, O Rāma, unless fallen, those two must not be abandoned by the king; / by abandoning them, O best of kings, loss of the kingdom is indicated,
and an evil destination in the other world for a long time, beyond doubt. / But a royal priest who opposes the astrologer must be abandoned by the king. / Otherwise, the royal priest is to the king like a mother, like a father; / he averts his undesired misfortune arising from divine afflictions.
Where could expiation be possible for the king [if he harms] that brahmin, / so long as the wise astrologer and royal priest are not maintained by the king?
If their livelihood is cut off, the king’s family goes to hell / for three generations; therefore, he should always avoid cutting off their livelihood.
An allotment of immovable property, in particular, should be made to both of them / in suitable proportion, O knower of dharma, to the astrologer and royal priest.

2.1.d:
भाव्यं सदा भार्गववंशचन्द्र पुरोहितस्यात्मसमस्य राज्ञा ॥
राज्ञो यथापि स्वजनेन भाव्यो विद्वान्प्रभुः स्यान्नृपतेः पुरोधाः ॥ 14 ॥ ॥
2.1.m: A king must always look upon a royal priest who is his equal like his very self, O moon of the Bhṛgu race; / just as the king should be treated with affection by his own people, so the learned royal priest should be a master to the king.

2.2.m: generous, possessed of great energy, devoted to his master, pleasant-spoken, / knowing completely the statecraft taught by Bṛhaspati and Uśanas.

rāgadveṣeṇa yatkāryaṃ na vadanti mahīkṣitaḥ ..
lokāpavādādrājārthe bhayaṃ yasya na jāyate .. 3 ..

रागद्वेषेण यत्कार्यं न वदन्ति महीक्षितः ॥
लोकापवादाद्राजार्थे भयं यस्य न जायते ॥ 3 ॥
2.2.m: Whatever kings do not say out of passion or hatred, [he conveys]; / one in whom no fear arises on the king's account from public censure;

kleśakṣamastathā yaśca vijitātmā jitendriyaḥ ..
gūḍhamantraśca dakṣaśca prājño bhaktajanapriyaḥ .. 4 ..

क्लेशक्षमस्तथा यश्च विजितात्मा जितेन्द्रियः ॥
गूढमन्त्रश्च दक्षश्च प्राज्ञो भक्तजनप्रियः ॥ 4 ॥
2.2.m: patient under hardship, self-controlled, with subdued senses, / of secret counsel, capable, wise, dear to devoted people;

इङ्गिताकारतत्त्वज्ञ ऊहापोहविशारदः ॥
शूरश्च कृतविद्यश्च न च मानी विमत्सरः ॥ 5 ॥
2.2.m: knowing the true nature of gestures and expressions, skilled in reasoning and deduction, / heroic, educated, neither haughty nor envious;

cārapracārakuśalaḥ praṇidhipraṇayātmavān ..
ṣāḍguṇyavidhitattvajña upāyakuśalastathā .. 6 ..

षाड्गुण्यविधितत्त्वज्ञ उपायकुशलस्तथा ॥ 6 ॥
2.2.m: expert in deploying spies, having an affectionate regard for secret agents, / knowing the rules of the sixfold foreign policy, and skilled in diplomatic means;

वक्ता विधाता कार्याणां नैव कार्यातिपातिता ॥
समश्च राजभृत्यानां तथैव च गुणप्रियः ॥ 7 ॥
2.2.m: eloquent, an executor of affairs, never missing the right time for actions, / impartial toward the king's servants, and fond of virtue;

2.2.s:
kālajñaḥ samayajñaśca kṛtajñaśca janapriyaḥ ..
kṛtānāmakṛtānāñca karmaṇāṃ cānvavekṣitā.. 8 ..
2.2.d:
कालज्ञः समयज्ञश्च कृतज्ञश्च जनप्रियः ॥
कृतानामकृतानाञ्च कर्मणां चान्ववेक्षिता॥ 8 ॥
2.2.m: knowing the proper times and seasons, grateful, loved by the people, / an overseer of works accomplished and unaccomplished;

2.2.s:
yathānurūpamarhāṇāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ niyojitā ..
rājñaḥ parokṣe kāryāṇi samparāye bhṛgūttama .. 9 ..
2.2.d:

दूतादिप्रेषणकरी राजद्वारेषु सर्वदा ॥
तद्द्वारेण नरेद्राणां कार्यज्ञा च विशेषतः ॥ 7 ॥
एवंगुणगणोपेता नरेन्द्रेण सहानघा ॥

एवं यदा यस्य भवेच्च पत्नी नरेन्द्रचन्द्रस्य महानुभावा ॥
वृद्धिं व्रजेत्तस्य नृपस्य राष्ट्रं सचारकं नात्र विचारणास्ति॥9॥
इति श्रीविष्णुधर्मोत्तरे द्वितीयखण्डे मार्कण्डेयवज्रसंवादे अग्र्यमहिषीलक्षणं नाम सप्तमोऽध्यायः ॥ 7 ॥ ॥

राम उवाच ॥ पुरुषाणां तथा स्त्रीणां गजानां तुरगैस्सह ॥
वालव्यजनच्छत्राणां तथा भद्रासनस्य च ॥ 1 ॥
रत्नानां धनुषां चैव खड्गस्य च सुरात्मज ॥
लक्षणं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः ॥ 2 ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
आदावेव प्रवक्ष्यामि पुरुषाणां तु लक्षणम् ॥
निबोध तन्मे गदतो भृगुवंशाविवर्धन ॥ 3 ॥
2.2.m:
always sending messengers and agents to the royal gates; / and through them especially knowledgeable about the affairs of kings.
Endowed with such hosts of virtues, faultless, / she should be consecrated in the kingdom alongside the king, or by the king established in royal power.
When a noble-minded wife is like this for the moon among rulers of men, / the realm of that king, together with its populace, will prosper; on this there is no doubt.
Thus ends the seventh chapter, named 'Characteristics of the Chief Queen', in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the Second Book of the illustrious Viṣṇudharmottara.
2.8
Rāma said:
Of men and women, of elephants together with horses, / of chowries, umbrellas, and likewise of the royal throne,
and of jewels, bows, and swords, O son of a deity, / I desire to hear the characteristics; tell that to me who am asking.
Puṣkara said:
At the very beginning I shall explain the characteristics of men; / listen to that as I speak, O enhancer of the Bhṛgu lineage.

एकाधिको द्विशुक्लश्च त्रिभिर्व्याप्नोति यस्तथा ॥
त्रिवलीवाम्̐स्त्रिविनतः त्रिकालज्ञश्च भार्गव ॥ 4 ॥
पुरुषः स्यात्सुलक्षण्यो विपुलश्च तथा त्रिषु ॥
चतुर्लेखस्तथा यश्च तथैव च चतुःसमः ॥ 5 ॥
चतुष्किष्कुश्चतुर्दंष्ट्रश्चतुष्कृष्णस्तथैव च ॥
चतुर्गंधश्चतुर्ह्रस्वः पञ्चसूक्ष्मस्तथैव च ॥ 6 ॥
पञ्चदीर्घो भृगुश्रेष्ठ तथैव च षडुन्नतः ॥
सप्तस्नेहोऽष्टवंशश्च नव स्थानामलस्तथा ॥ 7 ॥
दशपद्मो दशबृहन्न्यग्रोधपरिमण्डलः ॥
चतुर्दशसमद्वन्द्वः षोडशाख्यश्च शस्यते ॥ 8 ॥
राम उवाच ॥
एकाधिकाद्या ये प्रोक्ताः पुरुषस्य त्वया गुणाः ॥
तानहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि यथावद्वरुणत्मज ॥ 9 ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
धर्मे चार्थे च कामे च जनः सर्वोऽभिषज्यते ॥
एकाधिकस्तु विज्ञेयो यस्तु धर्मे विशेषतः ॥ 1 0॥
2.2.m:
He who is superior in one, white in two, and who pervades by three, / having three folds, bowing threefold, and knowing the three times, O descendant of Bhṛgu,
that man would be endowed with auspicious marks, and broad in three, / and he who has four lines, and likewise he who is even in four,
measuring four cubits, having four prominent incisors, and having four dark features, / having four fragrances, having four short features, and likewise having five fine features,
having five long features, O best of the Bhṛgus, and likewise having six elevated features, / having seven glosses, eight backbones, and pure in nine places,
having ten lotus-like parts, ten large parts, symmetrical like a banyan tree, / having fourteen equal pairs, and termed sixteen-fold, is praised.
Rāma said:
These qualities of a man beginning with 'superior in one' which were spoken of by you, / those I desire to hear as they truly are, O son of Varuṇa.
Puṣkara said:
All people are attached to dharma, artha, and kāma; / but he who is especially attached to dharma is to be known as 'superior in one'.

तारकाभ्यां विना नेत्रे शुक्लाश्च दशनास्तथा ॥
द्वात्रिंशद्राम यस्य स्युर्द्विशुक्लः स तु कीर्तितः ॥ ॥11॥
उरो नाभिस्तथा सक्थिर्गंभीरा यस्य देहिनः ॥
प्रोच्यते स तु धर्मज्ञ त्रिगम्भीरो नरोत्तमः ॥
अनसूया दया क्षान्तिस्त्रिकमेकं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ ॥12॥
मङ्गलाचारसंस्पर्शः शौचं चेत्यपरं त्रयम् ॥
अनायासमकार्पण्यमैश्वर्यं च त्रयस्त्रिकाः॥
त्रिप्रलम्बो भुजाभ्यां तु वृषणेन च कीर्त्यते ॥
दिग्देशजातिसर्गैश्च तेजसा यशसा श्रिया ॥ 14 ॥

2.2.m: he who pervades, O best of the Bhṛgus, is remembered as 'pervading by three'. / He on whose belly are three deep folds,

2.2.m: he, O best of the Bhṛgus, is called that best of men 'possessing three folds'. / Bowing to the deities, to the twice-born, and likewise to elders,

2.2.m: such a man, O best descendant of Bhṛgu, is called 'bowing threefold' always. / Knowing the division of time for the fulfillment of dharma, wealth, and pleasure,

2.2.m: and pursuing them, that knower of dharma is called 'knower of the three times'. / He whose chest, forehead, and face are broad,

2.2.s:

2.2.m: that man, O best of the Bhṛgus, is called 'broad in three'. / Whose two hands and two feet are endowed with lines

2.2.s:

aṅgulyo hṛdayaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ kaṭiryasya tathā samāḥ ..20 ..

2.2.m: of flags, umbrellas, and the like, that man is designated 'having four lines'. / Whose fingers, chest, back, and waist are even,

2.2.m: that man, O best of the Bhṛgus, is declared 'even in four'. / Ninety-six finger-breadths in height, four cubits in measure,

2.2.s:

प्रमाणयोगाद्धर्मज्ञ चतुकिष्कुः स कीर्तितः ॥

2.2.m: from the fitness of measure, O knower of dharma, he is called 'measuring four cubits'. / Whose four corner teeth, shining like the moon, are slightly raised
